title: Unrealistic emissions scenarios help AI climate models prepare for unfamiliar futures
summary: MIT researchers with Imperial College London designed a small synthetic set of deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios to train climate emulators, which normally need six to eight full Earth system model runs that each take months. The method needs only one model run, and the emulator predicted unseen scenarios and local pollutant-control effects where traditional emulators failed. It was validated with a simple climate model rather than a full Earth system model, and the article reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.
ai_technology: Climate emulator trained on optimized synthetic scenarios

title: Signs of hypertension detected by a smartwatch
summary: Prospective study of 196 people at five US sites, compared with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure measurement: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity for screening, and 78.4% and 90.9% in the confirmatory test (48 participants). A feasibility study; it does not replace the cuff, and many cases are missed.

title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins
summary: Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. The paper appeared in Nature Communications on 25 August 2026 and the institutional release on 5 November. Lab experiments in yeast and human cells confirmed several of the partnerships; most predictions remain untested, and the disease links are potential targets, not established ones. Predictions are shared through the MitoMatch web tool.
organization: Texas A&M AgriLife Research and Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis

title: First 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle, with Claude
summary: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, reduced purification from about three days to about 90 minutes, and processed cryo-EM data into an initial model in 34 hours. The result is a particle made of 96 copies of a bacteriophage protein, with about 25% more internal volume than the mammalian version. Its biological function is unknown; this is a preprint, and Claude made errors that humans corrected.

title: Agentic cheminformatics: new macrocycles from literature analysis
summary: An agent using Cheminformatics Skills for Antigravity collected thousands of compounds analogous to crizotinib and lorlatinib, analyzed 568, and proposed new rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The proposals are computational hypotheses that still need to be synthesized and validated.

title: Writing seen in PHerc. 306B for the first time in 2000 years
summary: Vesuvius Challenge awarded a $50K First Letters Prize for scroll PHerc. 306B, where the winning submission reached the 10-character target and the papyrology team agreed on a reading, tentatively a Greek phrase with parallels in Aristotle and Philodemus. Ink was detected by multiplying two models (TRACE v3B and a fine-tuned A-hn). Letters remain faint, the readable area is small, and the work relied on hundreds of hours of manual labeling.
ai_technology: ML ink-detection models (TRACE v3B, A-hn) with VC3D GrowPatch

title: Evo 2 uses in-context learning to design de novo regulatory sequences with only tens of examples
summary: Arc Institute reports that Evo 2 designs functional regulatory sequences from 4 to 64 in-context examples without extra training, with 30-50% yield. Of nine AI-designed enhancers delivered by AAV to mice, seven drove detectable expression and two labeled layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons with 73% and 95% specificity. Results are bioRxiv preprints; in vivo work covers only layer 5 enhancers, and other designs (proteins, CRISPR loci, antibodies, phage genomes) are computational only.
ai_technology: Evo 2 (genomic language model); in-context learning; reinforcement learning post-training

title: Claude's early progress in drug development
summary: Anthropic reports early results with six partners: a CAR T-cell receptor design about 70% shorter that enabled immune cells to produce about 10 times more receptors; about 35,000 antibody designs in one month, yielding 20 candidates; and a document review that found all 11 human-identified issues plus seven more in 89% less time. The work is mostly preclinical and reported by Anthropic.

title: OpenAI presents three results in harmonic analysis, complexity, and quantum theory
summary: OpenAI announces results on local smoothing, a disproof of the exponential time hypothesis, and the construction of quantum field theories. The source presents these as research results to be understood with academic groups: physical artifacts are not yet public, and independent verification is not established here.

title: Chest X-rays and AI for tuberculosis screening
summary: Nexus AI says it has deployed Google Research's chest X-ray AI as a certified diagnostic tool at about 40 facilities in six countries: more than 25,000 X-rays assessed by over 90 clinicians, with response times under 45 seconds. These are author-reported deployment figures, with no sensitivity or patient outcome data; WHO and FDA approvals are still in progress.

title: ForTy 2020: global map of forest types at 10 meters
summary: A 10-meter map classifies each land area into six forest or land-use types (including primary forest, plantations, and tree crops), with an initial time series from 2017–2025. Validation across more than 9,000 sites identifies the correct type in 90% of cases and distinguishes forest from non-forest in 95%.
organization: Google DeepMind, Google Research, World Resources Institute, IIASA

title: AI-assisted ultrasound for dating pregnancy
summary: Prospective study of 385 pregnant women in Chicago and Nairobi: the model estimates gestational age from scans taken by minimally trained operators with a mean error of 4.18 days, non-inferior to the 4.48 days of expert sonographers. This is a non-inferiority result from only two sites, both relatively urban.
ai_technology: Ultrasound model for estimating gestational age

title: GPT-Rosalind agents connect genetic perturbations and neuronal signals
summary: Analysis of a CRISPR atlas of mouse brain cells identified differences between Tsc1 and Tsc2 and a possible relationship between DCTN1 and cholesterol regulation. Experts assessed the interpretations, but the proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses to be tested in new experiments.

title: Claude designs binders against five scorpion neurotoxins
summary: In a mostly autonomous 64-hour campaign, Claude designed minibinders against five neurotoxins. External labs tested 211 designs, 17 of which met the criteria; the best (Cn2-B1 and Cn2-B2) had affinities in the low nanomolar range. Only recombinant toxins were tested, with no neutralization tests in cells or animals; Anthropic does not claim to have produced an antivenom.

title: AI agents in the lab: aptamers and proteins designed in a closed loop
summary: AI agents designed DNA aptamers and protein binders, which were then tested in the lab over multiple rounds. Target success rates reached 33.5% for myoglobin and 42.1% for α-thrombin (98.5% specificity). The post summarizes three arXiv papers whose peer review is unconfirmed; it also reports initial failures.

title: Claude designs more efficient quantum circuits
summary: Claude designed circuits for eight basic operations (chemistry, optimization, physical simulation, and number theory), assessed by an automated verifier. In several cases they outperform the best published circuits; for example, a point addition used 17 times fewer gates at the cost of 12% more qubits. Key identities were checked with simulation and Lean; a memory shortcut in the decoder fails about once in 10,000 times.

title: Searching for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
summary: An agentic workflow searched UniProt for antimicrobial candidates in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae and found a 97-amino-acid bacteriocin with no homologues among manually reviewed Swiss-Prot proteins. This is a computational candidate now undergoing laboratory validation; no potency or toxicity data are available.

title: Earth AI for public health: geospatial models across five use cases
summary: The PDFM model increased the explained variance in MMR vaccination coverage from 16% to 22% across 146 counties on the US–Canada border, and improved weekly correct cholera-risk-area rankings in the DRC from 1.78 to 2.10. Gains for cardiovascular mortality and postpartum depression were small or not significant.

title: SynthID Bio: watermarking for proteins and synthetic structures
summary: Methods insert a detectable signal into protein sequences and predicted structures. For binders designed against three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, and PD-L1), watermarked designs matched the others in success rate and affinity. This is a proof of concept that needs to be made more robust against tampering.

title: Catalysts without iridium or ruthenium for acidic oxygen evolution
summary: An AI-guided, human-supervised platform assessed 2,942 catalysts and identified complex palladium oxides. InMnPdOx maintained an overpotential below 0.5 V for more than 1,000 hours in sulfuric acid at 10 mA/cm². This is a preprint and laboratory result, without validation in a PEM electrolyzer.
ai_technology: Sequential learning, composition–property models, and LLMs

title: Claude identifies a new enzyme system: array-associated reverse transcriptases
summary: About 950 Claude agents searched a DNA-sequence database for 21 hours (210 million tokens) and flagged an uncharacterized enzyme system, found mostly in bacteriophages, with a DNA repeat array similar to CRISPR. Scientists performed the laboratory work; the function remains unknown, and the work is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication.

title: RetroChimera: predicting small-molecule synthesis
summary: Published in Nature, the method combines a Transformer model (R-SMILES 2) and a template-based graph model (NeuralLoc) through a learned vote. In blind tests with expert chemists, 90% of complete routes were accepted, compared with 20–50% for the component models or a baseline, and nine of ten difficult targets were solved. Evaluation covered only ten targets; one wrong prediction invalidates an entire route.

title: Claude optimizes more than 30 open models for biology
summary: In just under four weeks, Claude optimized over 30 models for structure, protein design, and genomics. They were on average four times faster with a small accuracy loss, and nearly twice as fast with identical outputs. It also created a low-memory mode for systems over 10,000 tokens on a single GPU node. Design results are in silico only, and comparisons are internal to Anthropic.

title: AlphaGenome Atlas: predictive map of human DNA variation
summary: A precomputed database of predicted molecular effects for about 9 billion possible single-letter changes in the human genome, generated by AlphaGenome. Researchers can access it free through a portal and API. The predictions are a research tool, do not replace experiments, and are not validated for clinical use.

title: OpenAI proposes a solution to the Navier–Stokes problem
summary: OpenAI announces a proof that three-dimensional solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations can develop a singularity in finite time and publishes a text formalized in Lean. This is the source's claim: this record does not establish community consensus, correctness of the artifacts, or recognition as a Millennium Prize problem.

title: Codex agents perform measurements and calibrations on a six-qubit chip
summary: Connected to MIT EQuS lab software, GPT-5.6 Sol selected parameters, ran measurements, and calibrated a six-qubit superconducting chip, measuring its frequencies and coherence. The demonstration covers known procedures on real hardware; weak or noisy signals sometimes required expert assistance, and no new physical property was demonstrated.

title: Claude formalizes Fermat's theorem in Lean
summary: A proof of Fermat's Last Theorem fully machine-verified in Lean: Claude produced most of it independently over 11 days, with about 13 million lines and 29,500 intermediate theorems, and a comparator confirms that its statement matches Mathlib's. It follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof, uses Mathlib and parts of an Imperial College project, and is probably longer than necessary.

title: WeatherNext 3: a global AI model for weather forecasting
summary: A model that learns from real-time geostationary satellite data and produces hourly forecasts, at resolutions down to 5 km for temperature and humidity (about five times finer than WeatherNext 2). For short-term precipitation, Google reports improvements of up to 60% over NASA's IMERG. These are ‘up to’ figures from Google's evaluations, with an independent ranking by Brightband.

title: Claude designs protein binders for 15 targets
summary: After an initial prompt, Claude selected binding sites, used design and folding models, and chose candidates, with success on 14 of 15 targets. Of 1,320 designs, 354 bound, for rates of 22–35% versus a typical 10–15%. None of the 90 designs for the maltose-binding protein worked. External labs ran the tests.

title: RAI-939: an autonomous-lab alloy tested with a torch
summary: Radical AI reports that AI-generated hypotheses and an autonomous lab produced new alloys, which were then tested by Purdue Applied Research Institute. During one minute under a torch, RAI-939 gained 0.25% mass while C103 lost 32%. This is a company announcement without peer review or replication details; scaling production remains to be developed.
organization: Radical AI and Purdue Applied Research Institute

title: WeatherNext Cyclones: forecasting cyclones one day earlier
summary: Three-day forecasts match what earlier models achieved at two days: about 100 km trajectory error and 11 knots intensity error, compared with ECMWF-ENS and HWRF. The work is with the National Hurricane Center, CIRA, and the Met Office. The comparison uses historical 2023–2024 cyclones; why results are good at 28 km remains an open question.

title: OpenAI presents ten results in mathematics and theoretical computer science
summary: OpenAI announces ten results on codes, non-sofic groups, arithmetic circuits, quantum games, lattices, and combinatorics, accompanied, according to the source, by Lean certificates. This record groups one announcement; it does not mean this collection independently verified ten results.

title: A quantum computer that learns from its own errors
summary: A reinforcement-learning agent tuned over 1,000 control parameters on the Willow chip: logical stability was 3.5 times higher under injected drift, with a further 20% reduction in logical error after expert calibration, and error below one per thousand cycles in the surface code. Drift was injected artificially, and scalability was shown only in simulation; published in Nature.

title: FastNet: physically realistic AI forecasts from the Met Office
summary: Trained with a loss function that preserves energy across scales, it reaches a mean squared error equal to the Met Office global model and exceeds it on some metrics, with more realistic storm cores in Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán. The announcement gives no figures, covers only two extreme cases, and the system is not operational.
organization: Met Office and Alan Turing Institute

title: A1: deep learning identifies an antibiotic candidate against gonorrhea
summary: A screen of about six million compounds found candidates active against resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. A1 reduced bacteria in animal models, and proteomics, genetics, and biochemistry confirmed its target, alanine racemase. These are preclinical results, published in Science Translational Medicine.

title: Genetic reanalysis assisted by o3 contributes to 18 diagnoses
summary: Among 376 unresolved cases, o3 Deep Research proposed explanations reviewed by specialists: 18 diagnoses were clinically confirmed, seven of which had already been established elsewhere but were missing from local records. This was a retrospective study across heterogeneous cohorts, without a measure of time saved or effect on care; clinicians made the decisions.
organization: OpenAI, Boston Children’s Hospital, and Harvard University

title: An AI system improves a Chan–Lam coupling reaction
summary: The system identified TEMPO as a useful additive for coupling primary sulfonamides; chemists reproduced yield improvements in 11 of 14 substrate pairs at bench scale. The work retains human supervision and specialized infrastructure; independent reproducibility and generalization remain to be checked.

title: ElectrolyteGPT can generate new formulations for battery development
summary: University of Chicago researchers trained a GPT model with a new notation (fLine) to generate complete battery electrolyte formulations, including solvent ratios, salt concentrations and temperature. Several AI-proposed compositions were synthesized and, per the release, performed on par with the state of the art in lithium metal batteries. No cycling or capacity figures are given, the work is early, and generated candidates still need experimental verification.
organization: University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering

title: OpenAI presents a disproof of the unit-distance conjecture
summary: OpenAI presents a construction of planar point configurations with more unit-distance pairs than predicted by the Erdős conjecture. The announcement says mathematicians outside the team checked it and provides a complementary explanation; this record checks the source, not an independent reconstruction of the proof.

title: Co-Scientist: repurposed drugs against liver fibrosis
summary: In Gary Peltz's Stanford lab, two of the three existing drugs proposed by Co-Scientist blocked fibrosis and promoted regeneration in human liver cells, while Peltz's own two choices showed no benefit. The anticancer drug vorinostat blocked 91% of a damage response that can lead to scarring. Cell experiments only; published in Advanced Science.

title: Co-Scientist and aging: metabolism and the integrated stress response
summary: Calico Life Sciences used Co-Scientist to formulate the hypothesis that metabolism regulates the cellular integrated stress response, refined experiments with the tool, and reports new findings. The post gives no numerical data, and the results have not yet been published or peer reviewed.
organization: Google DeepMind and Calico Life Sciences

title: Co-Scientist and ALS: hypotheses about RNA-based mechanisms
summary: Two groups, at MIT (Ritu Raman) and Boston Children's Hospital (Ryan Flynn), used Co-Scientist to assess a conflicting literature, turn ideas into testable hypotheses, and rank them by feasibility, focusing on RNA-based mechanisms and drugs. The post reports no quantitative results or experimental validation; the research is ongoing.
organization: Google DeepMind, MIT, and Boston Children's Hospital

title: Co-Scientist and molecular switches in severe infectious diseases
summary: Clare Bryant (Cambridge) used Co-Scientist, which ranked hypotheses and pointed to a protein she had not considered down to individual amino acids, to study molecular switches behind diseases such as sepsis. The lab expects to build cell lines with those mutations in about six months instead of two or three years; the hypotheses are not yet validated.
organization: Google DeepMind and University of Cambridge

title: Co-Scientist and mechanisms of metabolic steatohepatitis (MASH)
summary: Filippo Menolascina (Edinburgh) used Co-Scientist to search the literature for combinations of MASH therapies. The tool proposed the NLRP3 inflammasome as a link between inflammation and metabolism, and the post says the hypothesis was later tested experimentally. No numbers are given; the drug combinations were suggested for testing, not demonstrated.
organization: Google DeepMind and University of Edinburgh

title: Co-Scientist: genetic factors to rejuvenate cells
summary: Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg used Co-Scientist to search tens of thousands of papers, obtaining over 20 proposed genetic factors for reversing cellular aging, a couple of which were validated in the lab, and reducing analysis of genetic-screening data from six months to a few days. The post gives no sample size or peer review status.

title: WeatherNext and Hurricane Melissa: earlier warning in Jamaica
summary: WeatherNext forecast a Category 5 landfall in Jamaica five days ahead with 80% probability, rising to nearly 100% at three days. According to the post, it was the best single model for track and intensity in the National Hurricane Center's 2025 verification report, which used it alongside its HAFS model. The post gives no numerical comparisons; rapid intensification remains very hard to predict.

title: MatterSim and tantalum phosphide as a good heat conductor
summary: A candidate identified with MatterSim-v1, tetragonal tantalum phosphide, was synthesized and showed thermal conductivity of 152 W/m/K in the best samples, close to silicon. MatterSim-v1 inference is 3–5 times faster, and the new multi-task model MatterSim-MT predicts energies, forces, and properties. Battery and other property results are predictions, not experimental confirmations.

title: REDMOD: pancreatic cancer signals in CT scans taken before diagnosis
summary: Among nearly 2,000 abdominal CT scans originally considered normal, an AI radiomics model identified 73% of prediagnostic pancreatic cancers, with a median lead time of about 16 months. Validation included images from multiple institutions and protocols. This analysis used scans taken before diagnosis; clinical benefit and false positives in practice still need prospective evaluation.

title: GPT-5.5 and a proof about Ramsey numbers
summary: OpenAI reports that an internal version of GPT-5.5, with a purpose-built scaffold, found a proof of a known asymptotic result on off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, then verified in Lean. The announcement appeared with the model launch on April 23, 2026; the full proof is in a separate PDF now linked. Page rechecked November 12, 2026: the text matches.

title: Theoretical physics with Claude: the Sudakov shoulder in the C parameter
summary: Physicist Matthew Schwartz (Harvard) guided Claude Opus 4.5 through a resummation calculation for e+e− collisions, producing a paper with a new factorization theorem and testable predictions against data in about two weeks. Schwartz checked every step; the model claimed checks it had not done and made errors.

title: GPT-5.2 Pro extends a scattering-amplitude result to gravitons
summary: Building on work on gluons, GPT-5.2 Pro helped derive formulas for nonzero single-minus gravitational amplitudes in a special semi-collinear regime. The authors report analytical verification and checks against known physical limits; this is a theoretical preprint without experimental confirmation.

title: GPT-5.2 proposes a formula for nonzero gluon amplitudes
summary: GPT-5.2 conjectured a formula for gluon scattering amplitudes with a single negative helicity in a special semi-collinear regime. An internal model produced a proof that the authors analytically verified; the announcement describes a preprint, not experimental confirmation.

title: Gemini Deep Think on research problems in mathematics, physics, and computer science
summary: The Aletheia mathematical agent scored up to 90% on IMO-ProofBench Advanced and independently solved four open Erdős questions; work with experts covered 18 research problems, including a disproof of a submodular optimization conjecture. Its score on doctoral-level problems falls to about 38–46%; no result is claimed as a breakthrough, and the papers were submitted to journals.

title: Fel's conjecture proved and verified in Lean
summary: Axiom Prover generated a proof of Fel's conjecture on syzygies of numerical semigroups, verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib, without hints, lemmas, or manual corrections after the run began. This is a case study and an unreviewed preprint, with no data on attempts or time taken.

title: GPT-5 reduces the cost of cell-free protein synthesis
summary: A cycle between GPT-5 and a robotic lab explored over 36,000 compositions and reduced protein-production cost by 40% compared with the previous baseline. This is an experimental result in one CFPS setup; it does not establish the same reduction for other proteins, scales, or facilities.

title: DinoTracker: AI classifies dinosaur footprints
summary: An unsupervised model trained on nearly 2,000 fossil footprints and millions of simulated variations identifies eight features of variation and agrees with experts about 90% of the time. Some tracks over 200 million years old resemble bird feet, which could suggest bird origins tens of millions of years earlier. The interpretation is open: they could be early dinosaurs whose feet happened to look similar.
organization: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin and University of Edinburgh

title: AnomalyMatch finds over 1,300 unusual objects in the Hubble archive
summary: The neural network scanned about 100 million cutouts from the Hubble Legacy Archive in roughly two and a half days: nearly 1,400 anomalies were flagged and over 1,300 confirmed, including more than 800 not previously documented in the literature (mergers, lenses, and jellyfish galaxies). AI only ranks candidates; the two counts are not explained, and no false-positive rate is given.

title: Claude in biology labs: Biomni, MozzareLLM, and others
summary: Anthropic describes three cases: Biomni (Stanford) completed a GWAS analysis in 20 minutes in an initial trial and suggested new transcription factors in embryonic development; MozzareLLM (MIT and Whitehead) interprets gene clusters from CRISPR screens; a third lab is still testing. This is an Anthropic account without independent evaluation; some figures are estimates.

title: A double-Lambda hypernucleus of boron-13 found with deep learning
summary: Neural networks selected images from the J-PARC E07 emulsion plates; microscopy and kinematic analysis then confirmed an event as a double-Lambda hypernucleus of boron-13. The discovery comes from analysis of 0.2% of the emulsions and is based on a single event; published in Nature Communications.

title: NOAA puts three AI-based global models into operation
summary: AIGFS (retrained from GraphCast) uses up to 99.7% less computing than GFS (a 16-day forecast in about 40 minutes); AIGEFS has skill comparable to GEFS with 9% of the computing; and HGEFS (62 hybrid members) outperforms GEFS and AIGEFS on most metrics. Cyclone intensity worsened in AIGFS v1.0; the announcement gives no numerical scores.

title: GPT-5 and molecular cloning: 79-fold greater efficiency
summary: In a cycle with Red Queen Bio, GPT-5 optimized a cloning protocol, introducing RecA and gp32 as a new mechanism: 2.6-fold improvement with the enzymatic reaction, 36-fold with transformation, and 79-fold when combined. This applies to the model system used, with scientists carrying out the protocols; reported by OpenAI.

title: Graph neural networks identify oxides for hydrogen production
summary: A model of oxygen-vacancy properties selected twelve oxides to test for thermochemical hydrogen production; about 80% were active in experiments. Some were comparable to or better than the baseline only under certain reactor conditions; further study and optimization are needed.
ai_technology: Graph neural networks for crystal defects
organization: Sandia National Laboratories and HydroGEN collaborators

title: GPT-5.2 Pro and an open problem about learning curves
summary: GPT-5.2 Pro solved an open problem in statistical learning theory (learning curves are monotonic in the Gaussian case with known mean and unknown standard deviation), then extended it to higher dimensions. The authors checked the proof, including with outside experts. Reported by OpenAI.

title: Heat-resistant crops: a hybrid photosynthesis enzyme
summary: At Michigan State University, AlphaFold predicted the 3D structure of glycerate kinase in a crop and a heat-loving alga. Replacing three flexible loops with rigid loops from the alga produced a hybrid that remained stable up to 65 °C. The enzyme has not yet been tested in whole plants.
organization: Google DeepMind and Michigan State University

title: The structure of the LDL protein apoB100
summary: At the University of Missouri, Zachary Berndsen and Keith Cassidy used AlphaFold to predict the structure of apoB100, the scaffold of LDL particles, and refined it using cryo-electron microscopy data. The result is a cage-like shell with a ribbon belt. The post gives no figures such as resolution and no clinical validation.
organization: Google DeepMind and University of Missouri

title: Healthier bees: AlphaFold predicts vitellogenin's structure
summary: With the Norwegian University of Life Sciences, predicted structures of honeybee vitellogenin were confirmed by electron microscopy in July 2025; AlphaFold 3 helped study its interactions with other molecules. Early evidence suggests breeding times for resilient bees could fall from months to weeks, a still preliminary claim.
organization: Google DeepMind and Norwegian University of Life Sciences

title: popEVE: diagnosing rare developmental disorders
summary: Applied to about 30,000 patients with severe undiagnosed developmental disorders, it led to a diagnosis in about one-third of cases and identified variants in 123 previously unknown genes, 25 of which were independently confirmed by other labs. This is preliminary clinical use; further checks are needed before adoption, and the page gives no detailed metrics.

title: GPT-5 helps solve a 40-year-old problem about Nesterov's accelerated gradient
summary: Ernest Ryu (UCLA) proved why Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, introduced in 1983, remains stable despite the extra momentum that makes it faster. GPT-5's turning point was a rewrite of the equations: not correct as given, but with a structure Ryu then developed and proved himself, over about twelve hours across three days and after a dozen approaches. OpenAI's account says the model created no new mathematical tools and often produced plausible arguments that failed verification.
organization: OpenAI and University of California, Los Angeles

evidence.tested: Not reported
evidence.unknown: OpenAI states GPT-5 often produced plausible but flawed arguments; its restructuring suggestion was not correct as written. The proof was developed and written by Ryu. Whether peer review will confirm it is not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Per OpenAI, GPT-5 suggested approaches and restructured equations; Ryu checked each idea and wrote the final proof. About twelve hours over three days and nearly a dozen approaches. GPT-5 is not a co-author.

title: Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5
summary: A collection of case studies with universities and national labs in mathematics, physics, biology, computer science, astronomy, and materials. Examples: it helped complete a proof of an Erdős problem with Sawhney and Sellke, reconstructed the SL(2,R) symmetry of the Kerr wave equation, and proposed an immunology mechanism later confirmed by Unutmaz's lab. Reported by OpenAI; experts supervised the work.

evidence.tested: The OpenAI page lists case studies, for example a mannose rescue experiment in T cells whose results matched GPT-5 predictions, and Erdos Problem 848, where authors turned a GPT-5 density estimate into a full proof.
evidence.unknown: OpenAI says the cases are curated illustrations, not a systematic sample. GPT-5 can invent citations, mechanisms or proofs, and expert oversight is essential. One case reproduced an earlier published proof without citing it.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5 suggested ideas, mechanisms, literature links and experiments; scientists set questions, verified results and ran lab work. OpenAI says the model is not autonomous.

title: Kosmos: an AI scientist for autonomous discovery
summary: Each run reads about 1,500 papers and executes 42,000 lines of analysis code; outside scientists judged 79.4% of its conclusions accurate. Of seven discoveries, three reproduce results already obtained by humans and four are new. Limitations include spurious correlations, a cost of about $200 per run, and a six-month work gain estimated by beta users.
ai_technology: Kosmos (agents with a structured world model)

title: AlphaEvolve on 67 math problems with Terence Tao
summary: Tested on 67 problems in analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory, AlphaEvolve matched the best known solutions in most cases and improved them in several; in some cases it generalized finite instances into formulas valid for every input. Preprint not yet peer reviewed; source checked was only the team's article.
organization: Google DeepMind, Terence Tao, and Javier Gomez-Serrano

title: DeepSomatic: a neural network for somatic variants in tumors
summary: For insertions and deletions, it reaches 90% with Illumina data versus 80% for the best other tool, and over 80% with PacBio versus under 50%. In eight pediatric leukemia samples, it recovered known variants and flagged ten new ones that have not been independently validated. The tool and CASTLE dataset are open.

title: C2S-Scale: a model-generated cancer hypothesis confirmed in cells
summary: The 27-billion-parameter single-cell model, built on Gemma with Yale, predicted that silmitasertib would increase antigen presentation only in an immune-positive context. In human neuroendocrine cell models with low-dose interferon, the increase was about 50%. Validation is in cells only; the authors call this ‘a first step.’

title: Enterololin: AI helps clarify an antibiotic and its mechanism
summary: An AI screen of over 10,000 molecules identified enterololin, and DiffDock predicted its binding to LolCDE within minutes, confirmed by resistant E. coli mutants, RNA-seq, and CRISPR. The mechanism was clarified in about six months versus 18–24 with traditional methods. In mice, in Crohn's-like inflammation models, healing was faster than with vancomycin. Early stage; no human testing.

title: New families of unstable singularities in fluid equations
summary: Physics-informed neural networks trained to near machine precision revealed a new family of unstable singularities (blow-ups) in three fluid-dynamics equations, with a clear pattern between blow-up speed and instability order for the incompressible porous-medium and Boussinesq equations. Work with Brown, NYU, and Stanford: a step toward computer-assisted proofs, not a proof; the Navier–Stokes problem remains open.
organization: Google DeepMind, Brown University, NYU, and Stanford

title: First bacteriophage genomes designed by a genome language model
summary: The Arc Institute group used Evo to design genomes resembling that of phage ΦX174: of 285 designs, 16 yielded functional phages (67–392 mutations from the closest natural one; 13 had never-seen mutations). They infect only two E. coli strains; a cocktail overcame resistance in three evolved strains. bioRxiv preprint; peer review is unconfirmed.

title: Deep Loop Shaping reduces LIGO control noise
summary: The method, described in Science and tested at the Livingston site, reduced noise 30–100-fold in the observatory's most unstable feedback loop, in collaboration with LIGO, Caltech, and GSSI. The result covers one control loop; extending it to all loops and adding hundreds of events per year are projections.
organization: Google DeepMind, LIGO, Caltech, and GSSI

title: New combinations of additives for LNMO batteries found with machine learning
summary: A model trained on data for 28 additives predicted the performance of 125 new combinations and identified formulations that outperformed the initial ones in tests. The study concerns high-voltage LNMO batteries; the Argonne announcement, accessed via Newswise, does not quantify the improvement or describe industrial-scale validation.
ai_technology: Machine learning on molecular features of additives

title: GPT-4b micro: Yamanaka factor variants with over 50-fold higher expression
summary: OpenAI and Retro Biosciences used a specialized model to design Yamanaka factor variants that produced over 50-fold higher expression of reprogramming markers in vitro than controls, with results replicated across multiple donors, cell types, and delivery methods, and pluripotency confirmed. Reported by OpenAI; the model is not publicly available.

title: Antibiotics designed with generative AI against gonorrhea and MRSA
summary: Over 36 million possible compounds were screened computationally: candidate NG1 killed resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a dish and in a mouse model, while DN1 cleared a MRSA skin infection in mice. Only 2 of 80 fragment candidates could be synthesized; these are preclinical results.

evidence.tested: Generative models screened more than 10^7 chemical fragments in silico against N. gonorrhoeae or S. aureus, plus unconstrained design. Of 24 synthesized compounds, seven showed selective antibacterial activity; two leads reduced bacterial burden in mouse infection models.
evidence.unknown: Mouse results only; no human testing is stated. The paper's abstract was read, not the full text.
evidence.ai_role: Genetic algorithms and variational autoencoders generated fragment-based and de novo compounds; researchers synthesized and tested selected compounds.

title: Decoding inner speech with a brain-computer interface
summary: In four people with severe motor and speech impairments, researchers found imagined-speech signals in the motor cortex and decoded them with machine learning. They also tested filters and a trigger phrase to limit unintended decoding. This is a proof of principle with implanted electrodes: free, rapid inner speech cannot be decoded accurately, and attempted speech remains more accurate.

title: Perch: an open bioacoustics model to protect endangered species
summary: The updated Perch model, released openly, predicts bird species better than its predecessor and has nearly twice as much training data (birds, mammals, amphibians, and human noise). The post gives no numbers for the new model; results on Hawaiian honeycreeper detection are from the earlier model.

title: AlphaEarth Foundations: a 10-meter map of Earth
summary: A model combines optical, radar, 3D laser, and climate-simulation data into one representation for 10-meter squares, using 16 times less storage and with 24% lower average error than the compared models. The Google Earth Engine dataset has over 1.4 trillion embeddings per year and has been tried by more than 50 organizations. Benefits with LLM agents remain prospective.

evidence.tested: Compared against traditional methods and other AI mapping systems on land-use identification and surface-property estimation; average error 24% lower than the models tested, storage 16 times lower. Over 50 organizations tested the dataset; no sample sizes given.
evidence.unknown: The page states no limitations; it says the team is still exploring time-based capabilities and that embeddings may be more useful combined with reasoning LLM agents.
evidence.ai_role: The model turns satellite and Earth observation data into compact embeddings; scientists and partners use them to create maps and classify ecosystems.

title: Virtual Lab: AI agents design nanobodies against SARS-CoV-2
summary: A group of AI agents led by a principal agent designed 92 nanobodies: two bound to spike protein from recent variants in lab tests, and humans wrote about 1% of the conversation. Only 2 of 92 bound; the date is the Nature publication date given on the page.

evidence.tested: The Virtual Lab designed 92 nanobodies; experiments (multiplexed ELISA) showed a range of functional binders. Two showed improved binding to JN.1 or KP.3 while keeping strong binding to the ancestral spike protein.
evidence.unknown: The two are called candidates for further investigation. Neutralization and clinical use not reported in the abstract. Full text is paywalled; counts of tested designs beyond 92 and binding values were not read.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM principal investigator agent guided LLM scientist agents through meetings, with human feedback; they built a pipeline using ESM, AlphaFold-Multimer and Rosetta. Humans ran the experiments.

title: An autonomous platform speeds research on polymer mixtures
summary: The platform tests up to 700 mixtures a day (96 at a time), guided by a genetic algorithm: hundreds of mixtures outperformed the individual components, and the best retained 73% enzyme activity, 18% more than the best component. Application is limited to enzyme thermal stability, replenishment is still manual; published in Matter.

title: AutoBot: robotic optimization of halide perovskites
summary: A closed loop with robotics and Bayesian optimization explored a four-parameter synthesis space of over 5,000 combinations, and the model made predictions after sampling less than 1%; humidity during deposition was the most influential factor. This is process optimization, not a new material; the page gives no accuracy figure.

title: Aeneas: restoration, dating, and provenance of Latin inscriptions
summary: The model restores texts with 73% top-20 accuracy for gaps up to ten characters (58% when length is unknown), attributes provenance with 72% accuracy across 62 Roman provinces, and dates inscriptions within 13 years; it was trained on over 176,000 inscriptions. In a study with 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, results were best when parallels and predictions were used together. Published in Nature.

evidence.tested: Corpus of 176,861 Latin inscriptions. Aeneas: 72% geographical accuracy over 62 provinces; dating within 13 years on average; restoration character error rate 40.5% with known length. 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, solo versus with Aeneas parallels and predictions.
evidence.unknown: The paper notes a small dataset, survival bias, only about 5% of inscriptions with images, and weaker results where data are scarce. Training data include earlier editors' restorations. Other languages are suggested, not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Aeneas restored text, attributed provinces, estimated dates and retrieved parallels; historians evaluated outputs and combined them with their own knowledge.

title: Gemini Deep Think reaches gold-medal level at the 2025 IMO
summary: An advanced version of Gemini Deep Think solved 5 of 6 problems at the 2025 IMO, scoring 35 out of 42 and working in natural language within the 4.5-hour limit. IMO coordinators assessed and certified the score, while clarifying that they do not validate the system.

title: AlphaGenome: predicting the effects of DNA variants
summary: The model reads sequences up to 1 million base pairs and predicts thousands of gene-regulation properties at single-letter resolution. It outperformed the best external models in 22 of 24 sequence evaluations and matched or outperformed the best in 24 of 26 variant evaluations. Stated limits: distant regulatory elements; not validated for personal genomes or clinical use.

title: Skala: a deep-learning exchange-correlation functional
summary: It comes close to the 1 kcal/mol threshold on the W4-17 benchmark (0.85 kcal/mol on the single-reference subset) and is competitive with leading hybrid functionals on GMTKN55 at lower cost. It was trained on about 150,000 high-accuracy energy differences, roughly 100 times the previous dataset size. Accuracy is shown only within the training data's chemical space; it was not yet public at the time.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls redated with AI and radiocarbon
summary: The Enoch tool dated the writing of 135 manuscripts with about 79% agreement with palaeographers and roughly 30-year precision, following new radiocarbon dating; many scrolls appear older than expected. The 79% measures agreement with palaeographers, not accuracy against known dates; the announcement gives no details on training data.
organization: University of Groningen, Pisa, KU Leuven, and University of Southern Denmark

title: Rentosertib: AI-designed drug reports Phase IIa results in pulmonary fibrosis
summary: In the GENESIS-IPF study of 71 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis at 22 centers (placebo versus three doses, 12 weeks), the 60 mg/day group had a mean FVC change of +98.4 mL versus −20.3 mL for placebo. Groups were small, so larger studies are needed; biomarker analysis was exploratory.
ai_technology: Pharma.AI (generative AI for targets and molecules)

evidence.tested: Phase 2a, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 71 patients for 12 weeks. Primary endpoint (patients with at least one treatment-emergent adverse event) was similar across arms: 70.6% to 83.3%. Treatment-related serious adverse events were low and comparable.
evidence.unknown: Efficacy in larger and longer trials is not established by this phase 2a study.
evidence.ai_role: Generative AI was used to discover the TNIK target and the small-molecule inhibitor, per the paper's title and abstract.

title: Robin: ripasudil as a candidate for dry macular degeneration
summary: FutureHouse's multi-agent system generated hypotheses, experiments, and analyses and identified ripasudil, already used for glaucoma, as a candidate against dry macular degeneration. Lab testing of ten candidates found that a ROCK inhibitor increases phagocytosis by retinal pigment epithelial cells; human researchers carried out the experiments. Announced May 20, 2025, and published in Nature May 19, 2026. Preclinical data.

title: Microsoft Discovery: a PFAS-free refrigerant in about 200 hours
summary: Microsoft researchers used AI models and high-performance simulations to identify a prototype PFAS-free immersion coolant for data centers in about 200 hours, then synthesized it in under four months; initial tests of key properties match predictions. Microsoft describes it as an experiment still under analysis.
ai_technology: Microsoft Discovery (agentic orchestration and high-performance computing)

title: AlphaEvolve: an agent for designing algorithms
summary: An evolutionary agent based on Gemini and automated evaluators. It recovered an average of 0.7% of Google's computing resources, sped up a Gemini training kernel by 23%, and found an algorithm using 48 multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices. Across more than 50 open math problems, it matched the state of the art in about 75% and improved it in about 20%.

title: OMol25 and UMA: quantum-chemistry data and a universal model for atoms
summary: Meta released Open Molecules 2025, which it calls the largest and most varied set of high-accuracy quantum calculations for biomolecules, metal complexes, and electrolytes (about six billion compute hours), and UMA, an interatomic potential trained on over 30 billion atoms. The post gives no numerical accuracy values.

title: Aardvark Weather: end-to-end forecasting without a physical model
summary: A single AI model replaces the entire forecasting chain: it starts from satellite and station observations and produces global and local forecasts in minutes on a desktop using about one-tenth of the data; the page says it beats the US GFS on many variables. The announcement gives no metrics; it is not operational and depends on ERA5. Published in Nature.
organization: University of Cambridge, Alan Turing Institute, Microsoft Research, and ECMWF

title: DolphinGemma: a model for finding patterns in dolphin sounds
summary: A model with about 400 million parameters, trained on decades of recordings of Atlantic spotted dolphins from the Wild Dolphin Project, predicts subsequent sounds to identify recurring patterns; it runs on Pixel phones used in the field. The patterns have not been confirmed to carry meaning.
organization: Google, Georgia Tech, and Wild Dolphin Project

title: Seven organic-solar-cell molecules designed with generative models
summary: Generative and predictive models, refined with experts and experiments, suggested new non-fullerene acceptors for organic solar cells. Seven molecules were synthesized and tested, with efficiencies close to predictions; the news item gives no efficiency values or advantage over the best existing materials.
organization: A*STAR, National University of Singapore, and Elix

title: MICrONS: a map of one cubic millimeter of mouse visual cortex
summary: A map with over half a billion connections and about 75,000 reconstructed neurons from roughly 28,000 sections, produced over nine years by more than 150 researchers. AI traced every neuron outline, and the result requires human checking, much of which is already done. This is about one-thousandth of a mouse connectome, and cell counts vary within the text.
organization: Princeton University, Allen Institute, and Baylor College of Medicine

title: Euclid: 500 candidate strong gravitational lenses
summary: The first catalog of 500 candidate galaxy–galaxy lenses, almost all previously unknown, was selected with AI models and then reviewed by citizen scientists and experts. These are candidates, not confirmed lenses; 7,000 by the late-2026 release and about 100,000 by mission end are projections.

title: The AI Scientist-v2: a fully generated paper passes a workshop review
summary: A paper produced end to end by the system received a mean score of 6.33 at the ICBINB workshop at ICLR 2025, above the average acceptance threshold. Humans only supplied the topic and selected three papers to submit, and the accepted one was withdrawn. Only one of three cleared the threshold; it was a workshop, not the main conference, and there was no meta-review.

title: ECMWF puts AI forecasts (AIFS) into operation
summary: The European center operationalized AIFS Single on February 25, 2025, alongside the physical IFS model. ECMWF reports gains of up to 20% on tropical-cyclone tracks and about 1,000 times lower energy use. It is deterministic, at 28 km versus 9 km for IFS.

title: CorrDiff: kilometer-scale weather forecasts with generative AI
summary: A diffusion model takes atmospheric data from 25-kilometer to 2-kilometer scale and also predicts variables absent from the inputs, such as radar reflectivity. The paper appeared the same day in Communications Earth and Environment; the initial model was tuned on Taiwan data with the Central Weather Administration, and Taiwan's disaster-reduction center uses it for alerts. NVIDIA claims 500 times faster and 10,000 times more energy-efficient than high-resolution numerical forecasting on CPU: company figures, with no accuracy comparison on the page.

title: BioEmu-1: ensembles of protein structures with deep learning
summary: An open-source model that generates thousands of protein structures per hour on a GPU and reproduces the equilibrium distribution of a molecular-dynamics simulation using 10,000 to 100,000 times fewer GPU-hours. Predicted folding free energies correlate well with experimental values. The authors call it ‘a first step.’

title: AI co-scientist: a multi-agent system for generating hypotheses
summary: A system based on Gemini 2.0 that generates hypotheses and research proposals. In the lab, three drugs it suggested for repurposing against acute myeloid leukemia reduced cancer-cell viability, and all suggested treatments for liver fibrosis showed activity. Expert assessments covered only 11 targets; fibrosis results awaited a Stanford report.

evidence.tested: Elo auto-evaluation over 203 research goals; 15 expert-curated goals; blinded experts rated 11 goals (preference rank 2.36). In vitro on four AML cell lines: binimetinib, pacritinib, cerivastatin reduced viability; KIRA6 IC50 10 nM in KG-1a versus 180 nM in TK6. Seven combinations tested.
evidence.unknown: The paper calls validation preliminary and in vitro only. KIRA6 was far less effective in MOLM-13 and HL-60. Expert evaluation was small and subjective; Elo is not ground truth. Liver fibrosis and AMR details are summarized only.
evidence.ai_role: A Gemini-based multi-agent system generated, debated and ranked hypotheses; experts selected candidates and prioritized lab experiments.

title: Evo 2: the largest AI model for biology
summary: Trained on more than 9.3 trillion nucleotides from over 128,000 genomes, it reads sequences up to 1 million nucleotides, flags harmful mutations, and designs genetic elements and genomes as long as those of simple bacteria. In BRCA1 tests it exceeds 90% accuracy in distinguishing benign from potentially pathogenic variants (a result limited to that gene). Preprint; human pathogens were excluded from training.

title: Two molecules against KRAS from a hybrid AI and quantum process
summary: A process combining quantum and classical computing with Chemistry42 selected 15 candidates; two showed activity against mutated KRAS variants in living cells. Published in Nature Biotechnology, this is a proof of principle, with no significant quantum advantage or demonstrated superiority over compounds obtained by classical methods.
organization: University of Toronto and Insilico Medicine

title: MaSIF designs binders for protein–drug complexes
summary: MaSIF designed proteins that recognize three complexes containing progesterone, venetoclax, or actinonin, then validated them in the lab. A venetoclax-inducible system activated the antitumor activity of CAR T cells in vitro; this is a proof of concept without clinical validation.

title: MatterGen: materials design with a generative model
summary: A diffusion model trained on 608,000 stable materials. Compound TaCr2O6, generated with a constraint of 200 GPa bulk modulus, was synthesized and measured at 169 GPa (relative error under 20%), but with Ta–Cr disorder differing from the proposed structure. One experimental example.

title: Computer-designed proteins neutralize snake toxins
summary: Small, stable proteins designed with AI bind and neutralize three-finger toxins from cobras and mambas in the lab; in mice, they yield 80–100% survival against lethal neurotoxin doses, depending on the toxin. Laboratory and animal studies only; traditional antivenoms remain central.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: PRAIM: AI finds more breast cancers in German screening
summary: In a prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites, AI-assisted reading detected 6.7 cancers per thousand exams versus 5.7 without AI. Recall rates for further assessment were 37.4 versus 38.3 per thousand. This observational study does not show a survival benefit, and estimates of workload reduction with automated reading come from simulations.
organization: Universität zu Lübeck, UKSH, and Vara

title: Boltz-1: an open model for biomolecular structures
summary: A fully open MIT model predicts 3D structures of proteins and other biomolecules and, according to its developers, matches AlphaFold3's accuracy; unlike AlphaFold3, its training pipeline is also released. The comparison is developer-reported; the group calls it a starting point for the community.

title: GenCast: ensemble weather forecasts with a diffusion model
summary: A 0.25° model that outperformed ECMWF's ENS ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 variable-and-lead-time combinations (99.8% beyond 36 hours) and produces a 15-day ensemble in about 8 minutes on a TPU. Physical models remain essential because they provide training data and initial conditions.

title: AlphaQubit: a neural decoder for quantum error correction
summary: A Transformer-based decoder trained on data from a 49-qubit Sycamore processor made 6% fewer errors than tensor-network methods and 30% fewer than correlated matching in the largest experiments. It is too slow for real-time error correction on fast superconducting processors.
organization: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI

evidence.tested: On Sycamore data, logical error per round was 2.901e-2 (distance 3) and 2.748e-2 (distance 5), versus 3.028e-2 and 2.915e-2 for a tensor-network decoder. Simulations to distance 11 (241 qubits); correlated matching was 1.25 to 1.4 times worse.
evidence.unknown: Throughput is slower than the 1 microsecond per round target. Training at distance 11 needs more data. Accuracy beyond distance 11 and logical computations remain future work. Larger-distance results are simulated.
evidence.ai_role: A recurrent transformer neural network decodes surface-code syndromes to predict logical errors; it is the method under test.

title: OCx24: experimental catalysts for evaluating prediction models
summary: A dataset from Meta FAIR, the University of Toronto, and VSParticle covers over 600 mixed-metal catalysts made from 13 elements and tested under the same conditions, alongside analysis of over 19,000 materials. Hydrogen-evolution predictions flagged platinum-containing alloys as promising, although platinum was absent from training data. Fewer than 25% of produced catalysts matched the target; this was a pilot.
organization: Meta AI, University of Toronto, and VSParticle

title: Evo: a foundation model for DNA, from molecules to genomes
summary: Published in Science, Evo (Arc Institute, Stanford, and UC Berkeley) designed EvoCas9-1, a CRISPR system sharing only about 73% of its sequence with CRISPR-Cas9 but with comparable activity after eleven designs, and new IS200/IS605 transposons that cut and paste DNA. The team calls this the beginning and conducted an ethics and safety study.
organization: Arc Institute, Stanford, and UC Berkeley

title: Seven-day flood forecasts with reliability similar to earlier five-day forecasts
summary: The new model, trained on 15,980 stations (up from 5,680), gives seven-day reliability comparable to the previous model's five-day forecast. Flood Hub covers over 100 countries and about 700 million people (up from 460 million). About 250,000 virtual points are unverified and intended for experts only; flash, urban, and coastal floods remain out of scope.

title: NatureLM-audio: an audio-language model for bioacoustics
summary: Based on an audio encoder and LLaMA 3.1-8B, the model gives the correct scientific name about 20% of the time across 200 unseen species and counts zebra finch calls at 38.3% versus a 25% baseline; it is state of the art on most BEANS-Zero benchmark tasks. Early, modest results on the authors' own benchmark; preprint.

title: Mobile autonomous robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
summary: Mobile robots move samples between a synthesis platform, a UPLC-MS spectrometer, and a benchtop NMR, while a heuristic decision-maker evaluates data and chooses reactions. Demonstrated on structural diversification, supramolecular chemistry, and photochemical synthesis. The AI is heuristic and there is no speed or accuracy metric; the announcement says robots will not have a ‘Eureka’ moment.

title: FlyWire: the complete map of neurons in the Drosophila brain
summary: Connectome of the adult Drosophila brain: nearly 140,000 neurons, over 15 million synaptic connections, and over 8,000 cell types. The page says deep neural networks segmented images and extracted neurons, but automated segmentation had millions of errors and required about 33 years of human correction across over 50 labs and citizen scientists.
organization: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Princeton, and FlyWire

title: TxGNN: repurposing existing drugs for rare diseases
summary: The model covers about 8,000 drugs across 17,080 diseases and is nearly 50% better than competitors at identifying candidates and 35% more accurate on contraindications. It was tested on 1.2 million medical records and on three rare diseases excluded from training. Computational predictions only, with no laboratory or clinical confirmation.

title: Nazca: AI helps discover 303 new figurative geoglyphs
summary: An IBM model flagged 1,309 candidates; about a quarter were ground-checked over roughly six months, finding 303 new figurative geoglyphs among 430 already known and increasing the discovery rate 16-fold. Another 968 candidates remain to be checked; the study had been accepted by PNAS at the time of the announcement.

title: Solvent mixtures for flow batteries found through an AI–experiment cycle
summary: PNNL and Argonne identified solvent mixtures that dissolve three times more than a compound proposed for flow batteries, exploring less than 10% of about 2,000 combinations. The model receives experimental data and guides subsequent experiments; the result concerns solubility, without demonstrating performance of a complete battery.
ai_technology: Machine learning in a loop with high-throughput experiments
organization: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Active learning guided solubility measurements of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole in binary solvents: 218 measurements from 2,101 candidates found 18 mixtures above 6.20 M; best 6.50 M. On a 98-solvent set, Bayesian optimization needed 17 ± 11 trials versus about 50 ± 27 random.
evidence.unknown: Tested one solute, binary solvents only; solubility is not the only property and viscosity, conductivity and stability were not optimized. Model accuracy on 40 test solvents was R2 = 0.63. Real battery performance not reported.
evidence.ai_role: A Gaussian process model with an expected-improvement rule chose which solvents to measure; a robotic platform prepared samples and NMR measured solubility; humans selected features and candidate lists.

title: AlphaProteo: AI-designed protein binders
summary: A system for designing high-affinity protein binders, tested against seven targets, achieved 88% laboratory success on BHRF1 and bindings 3 to 300 times stronger than the best existing methods. It produced no valid binders for TNFα; strong binding is only a first step.

title: CHIEF: detecting cancer and predicting survival from slides
summary: Trained on 15 million patches and 60,000 slides and tested on more than 19,400 slides from 32 datasets and 24 hospitals: it detects cancer with about 94% accuracy across 15 datasets, predicts mutations in 54 genes with over 70% accuracy, and improves survival prediction by 8% across 17 institutions. Retrospective validation; not trained on rare diseases or premalignant tissue.

title: A speech neuroprosthesis reaches 97.5% accuracy after calibration
summary: A man with ALS used a brain-computer interface with machine learning to turn attempted speech into text and synthetic voice. After further training, the system maintained 97.5% accuracy; the study reports more than 248 hours of spontaneous conversation over 32 weeks. Result from one participant with an invasive implant; still experimental.
ai_technology: Neural speech decoding with machine learning

title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2: silver-medal level at the Math Olympiad
summary: The two systems solved 4 of 6 problems at IMO 2024, scoring 28 of 42 points, one point below the gold threshold. Problems were manually translated into formal language, and some required up to three days of computation instead of the official 4.5 hours.

title: NeuralGCM: a hybrid physics-and-learning model for weather and climate
summary: At 1.4° resolution, the model outperformed ECMWF-ENS in 95% of cases for forecasts from 2 to 15 days; at 2.8°, its mean 1980–2020 temperature error was 0.25 °C versus 0.75 °C for atmosphere-only models. It is more than 3,500 times faster than X-SHiELD on a TPU. It models only the atmosphere and is not yet a complete climate model.
ai_technology: NeuralGCM (differentiable dynamical core and neural networks)

title: ESM3 and esmGFP: a fluorescent protein designed by a language model
summary: ESM3 designed esmGFP, a fluorescent protein of 229 amino acids with 96 mutations relative to the closest known protein (about 58% similarity). In a second round of 96 designs, some proteins glowed as brightly as natural GFPs. The comparison with ‘more than 500 million years of evolution’ is an analogy-based estimate.

title: African elephants address one another with calls resembling names
summary: About 470 calls from 101 callers to 117 recipients in Kenya: a model trained only on acoustic structure identifies the intended recipient, and playback experiments show elephants respond more to calls addressed to them. The model confirms a previously suspected pattern; more data are needed to isolate the ‘names’.
organization: Colorado State University, Save the Elephants and ElephantVoices

title: AMPSphere: antimicrobial peptides from the global microbiome
summary: Machine learning identified 863,498 candidate sequences in microbial genomes and metagenomes. Of 100 synthesized peptides, 63 inhibited at least one of the eleven strains tested; some showed activity in animal models. The catalog contains candidates, not hundreds of thousands of clinically validated antibiotics.

title: Aurora: a foundation model for the atmosphere
summary: A 1.3-billion-parameter model for high-resolution weather and air-pollution forecasting: it matches or exceeds CAMS on 74% of targets and matches or beats GraphCast on 94%. The roughly 5,000-fold speedup over the IFS system is an estimate; GraphCast remains slightly better up to five days.

title: AlphaFold 3: structure and interactions of life’s molecules
summary: It predicts joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules and ions. DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs report at least 50% greater accuracy than existing methods for protein interactions with other molecules. Free for non-commercial research through the AlphaFold Server.

evidence.tested: Higher accuracy than docking tools for protein–ligand interactions, than nucleic-acid-specific predictors for protein–nucleic acid interactions, and than AlphaFold-Multimer v2.3 for antibody–antigen prediction.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy on new experimental targets beyond the benchmarks is not described in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion-based architecture predicting joint structures of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions and modified residues.

title: ChemCrow: a language-model agent with chemistry tools
summary: An agent with 18 tools and GPT-4 planned and carried out the synthesis of DEET and three thiourea organocatalysts on a cloud platform, and guided discovery of a chromophore absorbing at 336 nm against a 369 nm target; evaluated on 14 cases by four expert chemists. Hallucinations, limited tasks and dual-use risks; 12 of 18 tools were released.

title: Sperm whales: a possible ‘phonetic alphabet’ in their calls
summary: Analysis of nearly 9,000 codas from the eastern Caribbean clan, collected over more than ten years, proposes a combinatorial structure involving rhythm, tempo, rubato and ornamentation. Published in Nature Communications; communicative function remains unknown, data cover one clan, and the page does not specify machine-learning methods.

title: Closed-loop, distributed discovery of organic laser emitters
summary: In a two-month campaign, more than 1,000 candidates were synthesized and tested at six laboratories across five sites on three continents, identifying at least 21 high-performance candidates as gain materials from a space of more than 150,000 experiments. These are gain candidates, not confirmed lasers; the page gives no laser metrics; source is a consortium press release.

title: Protein-surface-designed molecules activate PPARs
summary: A generative model designed molecules from the three-dimensional surfaces of PPAR proteins: synthesized in the laboratory, they increased activity and were tested by Roche. They demonstrate the method and are not intended for commercial development; the tests do not establish safety or efficacy in humans.

title: OpenCRISPR-1: a genome editor designed by language models
summary: Profluent built an atlas of 5.1 million CRISPR-Cas proteins and generated a Cas9-like editor with 403 mutations relative to SpCas9. Of 48 generated sequences, the best (OpenCRISPR-1) achieved 55.7% on-target editing versus 48.3% for SpCas9, and 0.32% off-target editing versus 6.1%. Human cells in the laboratory only; company data; the page does not indicate peer review.

title: Antibodies designed from scratch with RFdiffusion
summary: Baker’s group showed RFdiffusion can be adapted to generate antibodies: in laboratory tests, designs bound influenza virus and other targets as intended. Proof-of-concept study, first circulated as a preprint in March 2024; experts quoted by Nature call it promising but an early step; no affinity values reported.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: AI identifies semapimod against dormant bacteria
summary: A machine-learning system selected semapimod, a known anti-inflammatory drug, for activity against dormant Gram-negative bacteria. MIT reports laboratory activity against E. coli and A. baumannii and an effect that sensitizes these bacteria to other antibiotics; the result is preclinical and does not demonstrate efficacy in patients.

title: SEEDS: weather ensembles generated with a diffusion model
summary: The model produces 256 members at 2° resolution every three minutes on a TPU and matches or exceeds the operational GEFS ensemble (31 members) on rank histograms, RMSE and CRPS. For the Lisbon heatwave (July 2022), with 16,384 members, none of GEFS’s 31 members was as warm as observed. One extreme case; depends on physics-based forecasts as seeds; published in Science Advances.

title: SyntheMol: generated antibiotic candidates against Acinetobacter baumannii
summary: The generative model proposed about 25,000 candidates in under nine hours from more than 130,000 synthesis building blocks; of 58 synthesized, six killed a drug-resistant A. baumannii strain and two were not toxic in mice. Mechanism unknown, efficacy in infected animals untested, and four of the six compounds were not water-soluble.

title: Reliable flood forecasts even where gauges are missing
summary: A model trained on 5,680 gauges improved average global forecast reliability from zero to five days: forecasts at days 4–5 were similar to or better than day-zero forecasts from GloFAS v4. Flood Hub covers more than 80 countries. F1 comparison across 2,092 basins for two-year return-period events; flash and urban floods remain to be covered.

title: Preventing tearing-mode instabilities in a tokamak with AI
summary: A model trained only on past experimental data predicts instabilities up to 300 ms ahead, and an AI controller adjusted plasma shape and beam power to avoid them in a real DIII-D experiment. The authors call it a proof of concept on one machine and one type of instability; paper published in Nature on February 21, 2024.
organization: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory and Princeton University

title: Vesuvius Challenge: the first Herculaneum scroll can be read
summary: The $700,000 prize went to a submission with 11 additional columns and more than 2,000 characters (about 5% of the first scroll), using models to detect ink and automated segmentation. Papyrologists evaluated 15 anonymized columns and recovered more text from the winning submission. Segmentation remains largely manual and costly.
ai_technology: Ink detection with vision models and automated segmentation

title: AlphaGeometry: Olympiad geometry without human demonstrations
summary: A language model proposing constructions and a symbolic engine deriving proofs solved 25 of 30 problems in the IMO-AG-30 benchmark (the previous method solved 10; the average gold medalist score was 25.9), trained on 100 million synthetic examples. It covers geometry only and a 30-problem benchmark.

title: From 32 million candidates to a new battery electrolyte
summary: With the PNNL laboratory, Microsoft screened 32.6 million materials using AI models and high-performance computing, narrowing them to 500,000, then 800, 150, and finally an electrolyte replacing some lithium with sodium (about 70% less lithium). PNNL synthesized it and built a working solid-state battery. Validation and optimization are ongoing; the post is by a Microsoft executive.
ai_technology: Azure Quantum Elements (AI and DFT simulations)

title: Satellite map of industrial activity at sea
summary: A model applied to about 2 million GB of Sentinel-1 radar imagery (2017–2021) maps vessels and infrastructure: about 75% of industrial fishing vessels are not publicly tracked, over 25% of shipping and energy activity is missing from AIS data, wind turbines more than doubled, and global fishing fell 12% during COVID. Published in Nature; ‘fishing’ classification is inferred; source is the organization’s own release.
organization: Global Fishing Watch, University of Wisconsin–Madison, Duke, UC Santa Barbara and SkyTruth

title: A new class of antibiotic candidates against MRSA
summary: A deep-learning model trained on about 39,000 compounds screened about 12 million commercial compounds; of about 280 purchased and tested, two from the same class reduced MRSA burden tenfold in two mouse models, with very low toxicity to human cells. Results from plates and mice; toxicity was partly predicted computationally.

title: Coscientist: autonomous chemical research with language models
summary: A GPT-4-guided system designs, plans and runs experiments using web search, documentation, code and laboratory automation, performing six tasks including optimization of palladium cross-coupling reactions. The abstract does not make clear which tasks used real hardware; only the abstract was reviewed.
organization: Carnegie Mellon University and Emerald Cloud Lab

title: Designed proteins bind peptides with the highest affinity reported
summary: Using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN, researchers designed proteins that bind helical peptides such as glucagon, neuropeptide Y and parathyroid hormone, with what the authors consider the highest reported affinity for a computer-generated biomolecule. They detect low concentrations of peptides in human serum and withstand heat; a parathyroid-hormone biosensor produced a 21-fold increase in bioluminescence. The press release gives no affinity values.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: FunSearch: new mathematical results with a language model
summary: A language model (PaLM 2) paired with an automatic evaluator found the largest cap sets on record in some dimensions, the biggest increase in 20 years, and bin-packing heuristics using fewer bins than established methods. The problem must first be expressed as code with an evaluation procedure.

title: MatterGen: stable materials generated from desired properties
summary: A diffusion model generates stable, novel materials directly from desired properties: 2.9 times more stable, novel and unique structures than CDVAE, and over 250 materials with bulk modulus above 400 GPa versus 2 in the reference dataset. Results were checked with DFT calculations; experimental verification remains the ultimate test.

title: GNoME: 2.2 million new predicted crystals
summary: A graph neural network predicted 2.2 million new crystals, including 380,000 of the most stable, raising the number of known stable materials from about 48,000 to 421,000. External laboratories synthesized 736 predicted structures. Stability is calculated and does not guarantee a material can be produced or will be useful.

title: A-Lab: an autonomous laboratory for synthesizing inorganic materials
summary: In the Nature paper, the autonomous lab made compounds from computed targets over 17 days of continuous operation. The original press release reported 41 of 58 (71%), while the author’s January 19, 2026 correction reports 36 of 57: on review, 36 of 40 claimed successes were confirmed, 4 were inconclusive from diffraction alone, and ‘new’ meant new to the platform, not to science. One compound was removed because it was in the training data.
ai_technology: A-Lab (autonomous lab with language models and active learning)
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and UC Berkeley

title: Chroma: a generative model for protein design
summary: Generate:Biomedicines published the Chroma model in Nature; it designs new proteins with requested biophysical, biological and therapeutic properties. The weights are freely available to academic and nonprofit researchers. The press release gives no experimental figures, and performance claims come from the company.

title: GraphCast: global 10-day weather forecasts
summary: It outperforms ECMWF’s HRES system on over 90% of 1,380 variables and test forecast lead times, and produces a 10-day forecast in under a minute on a single TPU. Comparison is limited to deterministic HRES; training uses ERA5 data.

evidence.tested: 10-day forecasts of hundreds of variables at 0.25° in under a minute; outperforms the most accurate operational deterministic systems on 90% of 1,380 verification targets; supports better tropical-cyclone, atmospheric-river and extreme-temperature prediction.
evidence.unknown: Comparison with ensemble systems is not described in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model trained directly on reanalysis data.

title: MetNet-3: short-range neural forecasts in Google products
summary: The model forecasts precipitation, temperature, wind and dew point up to 24 hours ahead at 1–4 km resolution, learning from about 1,000 stations, and outperforms HRRR and ENS in several regions. It operates in Google Search and the app in the United States and 27 European countries, with precipitation forecasts up to 12 hours. Preprint, no numerical values in the text and one case study.

title: Meta AI: near-real-time image decoding from brain activity
summary: A three-part system (image encoder, brain encoder, decoder) reconstructs viewed images from magnetoencephalography signals at each time point, with signals better aligned to DINOv2 than the other models compared. Images remain imperfect; fMRI decodes better; the page gives no numerical metrics; preprint.

evidence.tested: MEG recordings from healthy volunteers viewing images were decoded at each time point; several pretrained image models were compared (signals aligned best with DINOv2), and MEG decoding was compared with fMRI. Participant and image counts not stated on the blog.
evidence.unknown: Generated images are imperfect: high-level features are often kept but low-level features are often wrong. MEG decoding is less precise than fMRI decoding.
evidence.ai_role: AI models built the image representations and generated the output images; volunteers supplied the brain recordings.

title: Vesuvius Challenge: first letters read from an unopened Herculaneum scroll
summary: For the first time, a complete word (‘porphyras’, purple) was read from inside a never-opened carbonized scroll; a model trained on crack patterns yielded 13 letters independently and unanimously annotated by papyrologists. The letters are faint and lack context; other readings are not ruled out.

title: EVEscape: predicting viral variants before they emerge
summary: Starting from January 2020, the tool predicted SARS-CoV-2 mutations with accuracy similar to experimental antibody-binding assays and ranked their prevalence better; it generalizes to HIV and influenza. Retrospective validation; prospective performance is not reported.
organization: Harvard Medical School and University of Oxford

title: AlphaMissense: cataloging missense genetic mutations
