summary: It classified 89% of the 71 million possible missense variants: 32% as likely pathogenic and 57% as likely benign, with 90% precision on a database of known variants. Predictions are not intended for direct clinical use.

title: A neuroprosthesis translates attempted speech at 62 words per minute
summary: For a participant with ALS, intracortical electrodes and an AI algorithm converted attempted speech into text at 62 words per minute. With a 125,000-word vocabulary, the error rate was 23.8%, versus 9.1% for only 50 words. Proof of concept in one person, with an invasive implant and experimental device.
ai_technology: Neural network for phoneme decoding and language model

title: Woman with paralysis communicates through a brain-controlled avatar
summary: For a participant with stroke-related paralysis, an electrode array on the cortex and AI algorithms translated attempted speech into text, synthetic voice and avatar movements. Text reached nearly 80 words per minute after individual training. Experimental study in one person; the system requires a physical connection to computers.
ai_technology: Neural speech decoding and AI facial animation
organization: UC San Francisco and UC Berkeley

title: Neanderthal and Denisovan peptides reconstructed as antibiotic candidates
summary: AI analysis of proteins from extinct hominins identified sequences that were then synthesized and tested against pathogens in culture and in mice. Some peptides showed antimicrobial activity; these are preclinical results, with no demonstration of safety or efficacy in humans.

title: Avoiding aircraft contrails with AI forecasts
summary: In a trial with American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy, pilots flew 70 flights over six months using AI forecasts to avoid forming contrails, reducing them by 54% compared with flights without the forecasts. Flights that avoided contrails used 2% more fuel; across an airline’s flights, the impact could fall to 0.3% if only a small share need rerouting.
ai_technology: AI contrail-formation forecasts and satellite imagery
organization: Google Research, American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy

title: MASAI: AI-assisted mammography screening in a randomized trial
summary: In the initial analysis of 80,033 women, AI-assisted screening detected 244 cancers versus 203 with standard double reading and reduced the reading workload by 44%. A Lund update on January 30, 2026, after more than two years and about 106,000 women, reports higher sensitivity without more false positives. The comparison is in a Swedish setting; it does not demonstrate reduced mortality.
ai_technology: AI for mammogram triage and marking

title: RFdiffusion: designing new proteins with a diffusion model
summary: A guided diffusion model generates tailored protein structures, such as proteins that bind tightly to another molecule, and outperforms previous methods across a wide range of problems. The post says only that ‘a useful fraction’ of generated designs work as intended, without figures; the software was released in March 2023.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: Pangu-Weather: medium-range forecasts outperform the operational ECMWF model
summary: According to the authors, it is the first AI model to outperform ECMWF’s IFS at medium range: five-day Z500 RMSE of 296.7 versus 333.7, a global 24-hour forecast in 1.4 seconds on a GPU, and mean cyclone-track error of 120 km at three days versus 162 km. Source reviewed: Huawei Cloud blog, not the Nature paper (July 6, 2023); it underestimates extremes.

evidence.tested: Trained on 39 years of global data; stronger deterministic results on reanalysis data than ECMWF's operational IFS in all tested variables; also evaluated on extreme weather and ensemble forecasts.
evidence.unknown: Comparisons are initialized with reanalysis data, as the abstract states; performance from operational analyses is not given there.
evidence.ai_role: Three-dimensional deep networks with Earth-specific priors and hierarchical temporal aggregation.

title: NowcastNet: extreme-precipitation forecasts up to three hours ahead
summary: A model combining neural networks and physical constraints forecasts precipitation up to three hours ahead; 62 meteorologists preferred it in 71% of 2,400 evaluated events. Tsinghua reports it was already deployed on the National Meteorological Center’s operational SWAN 3.0 platform. Expert preference does not measure reduced damage or guarantee accuracy for every event.
organization: Tsinghua University / National Meteorological Center / UC Berkeley

title: CogSim helps predict fusion ignition at the NIF
summary: Neural networks, Bayesian inference and physics simulations helped assess, before the experiment, the NIF design that produced 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser energy delivered to the target on December 5, 2022. Experts designed the experiment; AI estimated its outcome and uncertainties. This is not the energy balance of the entire facility; the study was later published in Science in 2025.
ai_technology: CogSim (neural networks, transfer learning and Bayesian inference)

title: AlphaDev: reinforcement learning discovers faster sorting routines
summary: Working at the assembly-instruction level, the system found sorting routines up to 70% faster for sequences of 3–5 elements and about 1.7% faster for sequences over 250,000 elements; they were adopted in the LLVM libc++ standard library. A hashing algorithm 30% faster was added to Abseil. The largest gains are for short sequences.

evidence.tested: AlphaDev found sort 3 and sort 5 routines with fewer instructions than human benchmarks, matched sort 4, and had lower latency on variable sorts. Libc++ versions were up to 70% faster for five elements and about 1.7% faster above 250,000 elements.
evidence.unknown: Hashing result (30% faster) not seen in the text read. Search is at assembly level; the paper reports optimality proof only for sort 3 (17 instructions). Results cover tested CPUs: ARMv8, Intel Skylake, AMD Zen 2.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaDev, an AlphaZero-based reinforcement learning agent with a transformer encoder, built assembly programs instruction by instruction, rewarded for correctness and latency; the team translated results to C++.

title: Abaucin: a targeted antibiotic against Acinetobacter baumannii
summary: A model trained on about 7,500 compounds screened 6,680 new compounds in under two hours; of 240 tested in the laboratory, nine were antibiotics, including abaucin, which was effective against wound infections in mice. Activity is highly narrow (no effect on the other bacteria tested) and still preclinical.

title: ExoMiner and multiplicity validate 69 new exoplanets
summary: ExoMiner V1.2 combines deep learning with information about other signals in the same star system to validate 69 planets in Kepler data. This is statistical validation of transit signals, not new direct observation; the result is distinct from the 301 planets validated in 2021.

title: Nonlocal quantum interference without entanglement of intrinsic properties
summary: An AI- and graph-theory-based prediction was confirmed in two experiments: four photons exhibit nonlocal interference without requiring entanglement of their intrinsic properties. The superposition concerns their generation locations; applications to metrology remain prospective.
ai_technology: AI and graph theory for quantum experiments
organization: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Nanjing University and Hefei University

title: First draft of the human pangenome reference
summary: A consortium of 119 scientists from 60 institutions published in Nature a pangenome combining assembled genomes from 47 people of diverse ancestries, rather than one person. Google adapted DeepVariant to identify variants and DeepConsensus to correct sequencing errors; a long-read assembler achieved over 99.999% final accuracy. This is a draft: benefits for diagnosis and treatment remain prospective.
organization: Google Research and Human Pangenome Reference Consortium

title: New zirconium-indium-nickel superconductor identified with machine learning
summary: Predictive models and experts guided fabrication of candidates and identified a zirconium, indium and nickel alloy with a superconducting transition around 9 K. The press release reports a three-month discovery; this is not a room-temperature superconductor or a demonstration of industrial use.

title: LinearDesign: more stable mRNA sequences designed by an algorithm
summary: The algorithm, based on a parsing technique from natural-language processing, finds the most stable mRNA sequence for a given protein in about eleven minutes. According to Baidu’s press release, whose study appeared in Nature, sequences produced this way showed greater stability, protein expression and antibody response than comparators in animal experiments. Figures are company-reported; the Baidu release copy on EurekAlert was reviewed, not a baidu.com page.

title: An MRI decoder turns brain activity into text
summary: A noninvasive decoder reconstructs continuous text from fMRI that closely, and sometimes precisely, matches the original meaning in about half of trials (after dozens of hours of training with podcasts; it also works on silent videos). Published in Nature Neuroscience; it works only with cooperative participants and is not word-for-word transcription.

title: Language models guide improvements to seven antibodies
summary: Two rounds of laboratory evolution, using at most 20 variants per antibody, improved the affinity of four mature antibodies by up to sevenfold and three immature ones by up to 160-fold. Biochemical and pseudovirus tests; no demonstration of therapeutic benefit in humans.

title: PRIMO: a sharper image of the M87 black hole
summary: A machine-learning method trained on more than 30,000 simulated black-hole images reconstructed M87* from 2017 Event Horizon Telescope data, using the array’s full resolution: the ring is about half as wide as in the 2019 image. It fills gaps with patterns learned from simulations, without quantified uncertainty.
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology, Institute for Advanced Study and NSF NOIRLab

title: LuxSit: de novo luciferases active in the laboratory
summary: The group designed new luciferases and identified three active enzymes among the initial designs. The 117-residue LuxSit catalyzes blue light with the DTZ substrate; its function is verified in the laboratory, while therapeutic or industrial applications remain prospective.

title: Real-time wildfire perimeters from satellite imagery
summary: A model using geostationary imagery tracks fire perimeters with updates every 10–15 minutes and, according to the page, is more accurate than similar products and the previous model based on NOAA GOES-16/17 data; shown in Search and Maps for large fires in the United States, Mexico, much of Canada and Australia. Resolution is 2 km; clouds can hide fires; figures appear only in an image.

title: Deep learning searches for technosignatures around 820 nearby stars
summary: A deep-learning method analyzed 150 TB of Green Bank Telescope data from 820 stars, previously searched in 2017 without interesting signals, and found eight narrowband signals of interest with nonzero drift, present only in observations where the target was in view. Follow-up observations did not find them again; no claim of extraterrestrial origin.
organization: SETI Institute, Breakthrough Listen and University of Toronto

title: Sybil: lung-cancer risk prediction up to six years from a low-dose CT
summary: The model predicts risk from a single CT with a six-year C-index of 0.75 (NLST), 0.81 (MGH) and 0.80 (CGMH), and a one-year ROC area between 0.86 and 0.94. Retrospective validation on three independent datasets; trained only on smokers, with prospective testing and testing in nonsmokers as next steps.
organization: MIT, Mass General Cancer Center and Chang Gung Memorial Hospital

title: A liver-cancer target and molecule identified with Pharma.AI
summary: Pharma.AI combined PandaOmics, Chemistry42 and an AlphaFold-predicted structure to identify a hepatocellular-carcinoma target and produce a hit molecule within 30 days of target selection, synthesizing seven compounds. A second round produced a more potent hit; an early Chemical Science study, with no clinical efficacy demonstrated.
organization: University of Toronto, Insilico Medicine and collaborators

title: ESM Metagenomic Atlas: over 600 million protein structures
summary: Meta AI published predicted structures for almost the entire MGnify90 database (over 600 million), generated in about two weeks on roughly 2,000 GPUs with a 15-billion-parameter language model, up to 60 times faster than previous methods. These are predictions, and high-confidence structures are a much smaller subset.

title: AlphaTensor: new algorithms for matrix multiplication
summary: A reinforcement-learning agent found matrix-multiplication algorithms better than known ones for many sizes (for example, 76 multiplications instead of 80 for 4×5 by 5×5). Algorithms optimized for hardware were 10–20% faster on V100 GPUs and TPU v2. The improvement over Strassen applies in a finite field.

title: Machine learning and synthesis clarify metastable phases of carbon
summary: An algorithm constructed metastable phase diagrams of carbon and identified structural features of n-diamond that were then verified experimentally. The group also synthesized predicted phases and compared structures under a microscope; the work concerns carbon only and does not establish useful properties of the new materials.

evidence.tested: Workflow found 505 candidate carbon structures; a neural network trained on 273 phases, test error 37.1 meV/atom. Diamond-anvil laser-heating experiments on graphite with electron microscopy were used to compare predicted metastable phases, including n-diamond.
evidence.unknown: The search is not guaranteed exhaustive; the paper calls cubic-diaphite a candidate structure for n-diamond. The model had higher errors at high pressure; kinetics are only partly covered. Argonne synthesis of unreported phases was not seen in the paper text read.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicted Gibbs free energy; a support vector machine drew phase boundaries; an evolutionary search proposed structures. Humans ran the experiments.

title: AlphaFold helps interpret activation of PINK1, a Parkinson’s-linked protein
summary: After experimentally determining different forms of PINK1, the WEHI group used AlphaFold to model the human protein and its dimer, obtaining structures consistent with experimental results. The predictions also helped interpret how mutations associated with early-onset Parkinson’s may affect dimerization; this does not amount to a validated therapy.

title: ProteinMPNN: protein sequences designed in about one second
summary: A neural network generates the amino-acid sequence for a given protein shape in about one second, over 200 times faster than the best previous software, without specialist tuning. A related study shows that proteins designed with ProteinMPNN fold correctly much more often, including nanoscale rings and complex assemblies. Researchers describe it as the beginning of machine learning in protein design.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: AlphaFold Database: over 200 million structures
summary: The predicted-protein-structure archive, maintained with EMBL-EBI, grew from nearly 1 million to over 200 million structures, covering practically all cataloged proteins, with free access and bulk download from Google Cloud. More than 500,000 researchers in 190 countries had already used it. These are predictions, not experimental measurements.

title: TREWS: early sepsis alerts evaluated in five hospitals
summary: A machine-learning system monitored about 590,000 patients in five hospitals, flagging sepsis risk from medical records. In the studied cohort, timely clinical confirmation of alerts was associated with lower mortality, organ failure and length of stay. Observational study: the association does not show that AI caused better outcomes.
organization: Johns Hopkins University and Bayesian Health

title: BirdNET: citizen science through bird-song identification
summary: The app recognizes over 3,000 species from their calls, with more than 2.2 million people contributing since 2018; in four test cases, its data reproduced known patterns such as song distribution and the migration ranges of two species. Published in PLOS Biology; only four cases, with no identification-error figures.

title: Model of the human nuclear pore with AlphaFold2 and electron microscopy
summary: AlphaFold2 and ColabFold, combined with cryo-tomography and cryo-electron microscopy, produced a model of the human nuclear pore complex (about 30 proteins, about 1,000 copies, 120 MDa) covering over 90% of the complex, versus 46% for previous models. Flexible parts remain unresolved; a complete dynamic model is future work.

title: Machine learning suggests a more general theory of microlensing
summary: An algorithm highlighted microlensing configurations not explained by usual interpretations, leading to a theory unifying two degeneracies. The authors report a better fit to data from two dozen previous discoveries; they describe the theory as probably incomplete.
organization: UC Berkeley / The Ohio State University

title: FAST-PETase: an AI-engineered enzyme degrades PET waste
summary: A machine-learning model suggested PETase mutations, then tested on 51 post-consumer containers, fibers and fabrics. FAST-PETase degrades PET below 50 °C, in some cases down to monomers within 24 hours; production at scale and environmental use still needed development.

title: Murmurations: unexpected oscillations in elliptic-curve data
summary: Classification experiments and analysis of elliptic-curve data show oscillations in the mean of Frobenius traces that vary with rank. A numerical observation, not proof of a general law; the 2022 preprint was later published in Experimental Mathematics in 2024.
organization: Yang-Hui He, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Thomas Oliver and Alexey Pozdnyakov

title: Ithaca: restoring and dating ancient Greek inscriptions
summary: A neural network reconstructs missing text in damaged Greek inscriptions, identifies their provenance and dates them: 62% accuracy in restoration, 71% in location, and dating within 30 years of reference ranges. With Ithaca, historians improved from 25% to 72% correct restorations. It is intended to assist historians.

title: FourCastNet: high-resolution global forecasts with neural networks
summary: The preprint presents global forecasts at 0.25° resolution and a one-week forecast in under two seconds. Comparison with IFS is favorable at short lead times for large-scale variables and some finer-scale variables; this does not mean general superiority or operational use.

title: Tokamak plasma control with reinforcement learning
summary: A single neural network controls the magnetic coils of Lausanne’s TCV tokamak and forms plasmas in different configurations (snowflake, ITER-like shape, double droplet). Trained mainly in simulation and then tested on the real machine. Stated limitations: plasma lasts about three seconds and the machine changes from day to day.
organization: Google DeepMind and EPFL Swiss Plasma Center

evidence.tested: On the TCV tokamak the controller produced and held elongated, conventional, negative-triangularity and snowflake configurations, with accurate tracking of location, current and shape, and sustained two separate 'droplet' plasmas.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to larger or reactor-scale devices is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A deep reinforcement-learning architecture learned to command the full set of control coils from high-level objectives.

title: DINGO: gravitational-wave parameters in seconds
summary: The neural network estimates the mass, spin, position, inclination and distance of binary black holes in seconds rather than hours or months, with about ten days of training, and was tested on eight events from LIGO and Virgo’s O1 and O2 runs. Published in Physical Review Letters; extension to neutron stars is only promising; source reviewed was a Max Planck doctoral-program page.
organization: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

title: DM21: a neural network as a density-functional theory functional
summary: A neural network represents the functional used in DFT and addresses two longstanding errors of traditional functionals: excessive electron delocalization and spin-symmetry breaking during bond breaking. Published in Science with open code; the post gives no benchmark figures and DFT remains an approximation.
ai_technology: DM21 (neural network for the exchange-correlation functional)

title: AI-guided pure mathematics: knots and representation theory
summary: With mathematicians Williamson (Sydney) and Lackenby and Juhász (Oxford), supervised-learning techniques revealed patterns leading to an unexpected link between a knot’s algebraic signature and its geometry (the ‘natural slope’), and to a new algorithm for the combinatorial invariance conjecture. The conjectures and proofs are the mathematicians’; the algorithm was checked on over 3 million examples, not proved in general.

title: A neural network “hallucinates” new protein structures
summary: The network predicted about 2,000 new sequences as foldable; over 100 were produced in the lab, and for three, nuclear magnetic resonance and X-ray crystallography confirmed the predicted shapes. Only three proteins were characterized in detail; using the method to create useful functions (drugs, enzymes) is a future goal.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: ExoMiner: 301 new planets validated in Kepler data
summary: The ExoMiner neural network, run on the Pleiades supercomputer, validated 301 planets from the remaining Kepler candidates, adding to the 4,569 already validated; none is Earth-like or in the habitable zone. “Validated” is statistical, not confirmed; NASA’s 2026 count gives 370 for the same work, an unexplained discrepancy.
organization: NASA Ames Research Center and NASA JPL

title: Enformer: gene expression predicted from DNA sequence
summary: A Transformer-based model predicts gene expression from 200,000 base pairs of input DNA, over five times more than earlier methods, and is much more accurate at predicting variant effects. Enhancer attribution scores are comparable to methods using experimental data. The post gives no numerical gain and acknowledges that linking enhancers to the genes they regulate remains an open problem.

title: Short-term rainfall prediction with a generative model
summary: Developed with the UK Met Office, the model forecasts precipitation up to two hours ahead; over 50 expert meteorologists chose it as their first choice in 89% of cases compared with the most widely used methods. The authors cite long-range accuracy and rare, intense events as limitations.

title: Climate TRACE: first independent database of global emissions
summary: Using machine learning on data from over 300 satellites and 11,100 sensors (over 59 trillion bytes), emissions from oil and gas in major countries were estimated at about twice UNFCCC reports (about 1 billion tonnes more), while rice emissions in India were nearly three times the official 2016 inventory. No peer review; the page gives both September 14 and September 16, 2021.
ai_technology: Machine learning on satellite and sensor data

title: IceNet: seasonal forecasts of Arctic sea ice
summary: The model outperforms ECMWF’s SEAS5 dynamical system in seasonal forecasts of summer sea ice, especially for extreme events, and is over 2,000 times faster (under ten seconds on a GPU). SEAS5 is better at a one-month lead, and the September comparison covers nine years; published in Nature Communications.
organization: British Antarctic Survey, Alan Turing Institute, and others

title: INS018_073: AI identifies a preclinical candidate for renal fibrosis
summary: Insilico Medicine named INS018_073 a preclinical candidate after in vitro tests and testing in a mouse model of renal fibrosis. The company reports improvements in pathology, biomarkers, and histologically observed fibrosis. The candidate was proposed for IND-enabling studies; these are company-reported preclinical results, not clinical evidence or independent confirmation.

title: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database: first 350,000 models
summary: Predicted structures for the human proteome (about 20,000 proteins) and 20 other organisms were published, over 350,000 models in total, hosted free by EMBL-EBI. DeepMind announced an expansion to over 100 million structures. These are predictions that complement experimental methods. Note: the page header says July 22, 2022, but the text calls CASP14 “last December” and the 2022 post refers to it as a 2021 release; date corrected to 2021.

evidence.tested: Predictions cover 98.5% of human proteins; 58% of residues have a confident prediction and 36% very high confidence. Case studies illustrate possible hypotheses.
evidence.unknown: The structures are predictions; the abstract does not report experimental confirmation of new structures.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 2 applied at proteome scale, with confidence metrics built on the model.

title: ProGen generates artificial proteins with enzyme activity
summary: A protein language model generated synthetic lysozymes: two of the five characterized in cells degraded bacterial cell walls with activity comparable to egg-white lysozyme. Laboratory tests and crystallography support the result, but do not demonstrate clinical applications. The preprint dates to July 18, 2021; the Nature Biotechnology publication and UCSF announcement are from January 2023.

title: RoseTTAFold: accessible prediction of protein structures
summary: A three-track neural network (sequence, residue interactions, and 3D structure) computes a structure in about ten minutes on a single gaming computer. Baker’s group predicted hundreds of new structures, including little-known proteins in the human genome. The web server received over 4,500 requests in the previous month. The page does not state limitations.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: A neuroprosthesis restores words for a man with paralysis
summary: Neural networks decoded the attempted speech of a man with stroke-related paralysis, displaying words and sentences on a screen. With a 50-word vocabulary, the system reached up to 18 words per minute and a median accuracy of 75%. Proof of principle in one person, using an implant on the brain surface and a limited vocabulary.
ai_technology: Neural networks for speech and language model

title: H01: reconstruction of one cubic millimeter of human cerebral cortex
summary: A sample of about 1 mm³ of human cortex was imaged at 4 nm across about 5,300 sections and automatically reconstructed: 1.4 petabytes, tens of thousands of neurons, 130 million annotated synapses, and 104 manually corrected cells. The sample is about one-millionth of a brain; reconstruction is imperfect and initial findings are preliminary.
ai_technology: Automated segmentation of electron microscopy images

title: EAGLE: AI electrocardiograms to detect reduced heart function
summary: A randomized study across 120 primary-care groups at 45 sites evaluated neural-network alerts on electrocardiograms from 22,641 adults. The intervention produced five additional diagnoses of low ejection fraction per thousand patients, without a global increase in echocardiography use. The result concerns identification of dysfunction, not improved clinical outcomes.

title: Combinatorial constructions and counterexamples with neural networks
summary: The deep cross-entropy method (reinforcement learning) finds constructions and counterexamples to open conjectures in extremal combinatorics and graph theory, including a Brualdi–Cao question about permanents. The counterexamples are verifiable; source checked was only the arXiv paper, with no institutional announcement.

title: Two scribes in the Great Isaiah Scroll: new evidence from handwriting
summary: Independent analyses of character shapes distinguish two groups across the scroll’s 54 columns, consistent with two scribes alternating around the manuscript’s midpoint. This is statistical evidence from one artifact; the writers’ identities are unknown, and other explanations for the differences are not entirely ruled out.

title: IBM designs two new antimicrobial peptides with generative models
summary: Over 48 days, 20 candidates were designed, synthesized, and tested; two showed activity against several pathogens, including multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. In vitro and mouse tests only, with no demonstration of safety or efficacy in humans.

title: trRosetta releases over 6,300 predicted protein-family structures
summary: Over 6,300 protein structures predicted with deep learning are available in Pfam to explore families without a known structure. These are computational models with estimated quality, not newly experimentally determined structures; this result is distinct from RoseTTAFold and the AlphaFold Database.

title: Mirai: future breast cancer risk from mammograms
summary: Mirai, trained on over 200,000 exams, was evaluated on hospital data from the United States, Sweden, and Taiwan. In a comparison of high-risk groups at Massachusetts General Hospital, it identified nearly twice as many future diagnoses as Tyrer-Cuzick; it does not demonstrate reduced mortality.

title: Sequential X-rays to predict COVID-19 deterioration
summary: Models trained in part on 26,838 X-rays from 4,914 patients predict deterioration up to 96 hours ahead, outperforming specialists in some retrospective comparisons. This research is for hospital resource planning, not a clinical product or evidence of better patient outcomes.

title: Language models identify viral regions less prone to immune escape
summary: Analysis of influenza, HIV, and coronavirus sequences identifies regions of surface proteins less likely to mutate to escape immune responses, including the S2 subunit of spike. These are computational leads for studying possible vaccine targets, not validated vaccines.

title: 1,210 gravitational-lens candidates in the DESI Legacy Surveys
summary: Applied to DR8 data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, machine learning found 1,210 strong gravitational-lens candidates. The DESI collaboration says this is about twice the number of lenses known at the time; these are candidates, not objects individually confirmed in every case.
organization: NSF NOIRLab, University of San Francisco, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

title: AlphaFold wins CASP14 for protein folding
summary: AlphaFold achieved a median GDT score of 92.4 across the target set (about 1.6 Å mean error) and 87.0 on the hardest targets, which organizers judged a solution to the problem of single-protein structures. DeepMind notes that protein complexes and interactions with other molecules remain open challenges.

title: CAMEO discovers GST467, a phase-change material with double the optical contrast
summary: CAMEO, using Bayesian active learning and closed-loop X-ray measurements, identified the Ge4Sb6Te7 alloy in 19 experimental cycles (about 10 hours), selected from 177 compositions. GST467 showed twice the optical contrast of GST225 and was demonstrated in a phase-change memory device; the result concerns this library and application, not a commercial memory.
organization: NIST, University of Maryland, University of Washington, SLAC

title: A model analyzes coughs to detect COVID-19 infections
summary: A model trained on volunteer recordings recognized 98.5% of coughs associated with confirmed infections in the test reported by MIT. This is an early result on data collected online, with health status also self-reported; it is not a diagnosis or prospective clinical validation.

title: FermiNet: quantum physics of molecules from first principles
summary: A neural network for electron wavefunctions: for the smallest molecules it captures 99.8% of the correlation energy relative to a Slater determinant, at least 97% for bicyclobutane (30 electrons), and a mean error of 4 meV for excited states of the carbon dimer versus 20 meV for earlier methods. The page is dated 2024-08-22 but gives the original date as 2020-10-19; the method is approximate.

title: Over 1.8 billion trees mapped in Africa’s drylands
summary: Analysis of high-resolution images located and measured the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees across 1.3 million km² of West Africa. Validation used manual annotations and field data; the study counts trees but does not yet measure their stored carbon.

title: Chematica: computational synthesis planning for natural products
summary: The system plans multistep syntheses of complex natural products, with routes in a Turing-test study largely indistinguishable from human routes; three computer-designed syntheses were carried out in the lab: dauricine, tacamonidine, and lamellodysidine A. Based on over 100,000 rules plus AI, it is not modern generative AI.
organization: Polish Academy of Sciences, Northwestern University, IBS Center for Soft and Living Matter, and UNIST

evidence.tested: In a Turing-like test, synthesis experts largely could not distinguish the program's routes from human ones; three computer-designed natural-product syntheses were carried out in the lab.
evidence.unknown: How often its routes fail across other targets is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: The planning program combines chemistry knowledge, data-based AI routines and causal relationships to plan several steps ahead.

title: A mobile robotic chemist
summary: A mobile robot ran 688 experiments in eight days in a ten-variable space, guided by a batch Bayesian algorithm, to search for photocatalysts that produce hydrogen from water; the best mixtures were six times more active than the initial formulations. This optimizes a formulation, not a new structure; only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: Batch Bayesian optimization and mobile robot

title: AI and clinical data to identify COVID-19 from CT scans
summary: In a test on 279 patients, a system combining CT scans and clinical information reached 84% sensitivity, compared with 75% for radiologists in the reported comparison. Retrospective study on data collected in China, without evidence of effectiveness in prospective clinical use.

title: An AI system predicts progression of macular degeneration
summary: The system analyzes OCT scans to predict whether the less affected eye of patients with macular degeneration will develop the wet form, outperforming specialists in the comparison described. The announcement gives no numerical metrics; preventive clinical studies were still to be planned.

title: Cu–Al electrocatalysts for CO2 found with active learning
summary: DFT and active machine learning identified Cu–Al catalysts that reduce CO2 to ethylene with over 80% Faradaic efficiency at 400 mA/cm² (about 66% for pure copper) and 55% half-cell energy efficiency at 150 mA/cm². Synthesized and tested in the lab; the abstract does not state how many candidates were screened.

title: LCLS magnet tuning with machine learning
summary: A physics-informed Gaussian process using historical data tunes the accelerator’s 24 LCLS quadrupole magnets. The authors estimate tuning is about three to five times faster, with beams tending to be more intense; this is a result on the real machine, limited to this part of the tuning process.

title: Graph networks to understand glass dynamics
summary: The networks predict particle mobility in simulated glasses; perturbing the network reveals growing spatial correlations as the glass transition is approached. Evidence comes from simulations: the learned correlation length does not translate directly into a measurable physical quantity.

title: MetNet: neural rainfall forecasting up to 8 hours ahead
summary: The model forecasts precipitation at 1 km resolution and 2-minute intervals up to 8 hours ahead from radar and satellite, without physical equations. According to the page, it outperforms NOAA’s operational HRRR model up to about 7–8 hours, in seconds rather than about an hour. US coverage only, author-only comparisons, a preprint, and no stated operational use.

title: DeepScribe: reading cuneiform signs on Persepolis tablets
summary: A machine-learning model recognizes signs on tablets from the Persepolis Fortification Archive with about 80% accuracy on tablets excluded from training (over 6,000 annotated images and over 100,000 signs in the database). About 20% of signs are wrong; testing is internal only, and the source is a university announcement.

title: Predicted structures of SARS-CoV-2 proteins
summary: DeepMind openly shared AlphaFold predictions, without waiting for review, for six poorly studied viral proteins (membrane, ORF3a, Nsp2, Nsp4, Nsp6, and the C-terminal domain of papain-like protease). They were not experimentally verified; an ORF3a experimental structure deposited in the PDB in June 2020 matched the second predicted model well.

title: Halicin: deep learning identifies an antibiotic
summary: A model trained on about 2,500 molecules screened the roughly 6,000 compounds in the Broad Institute’s Drug Repurposing Hub and identified halicin, which killed many resistant bacteria in the lab and cleared A. baumannii infections in mice within 24 hours. Cell-culture and mouse results, not human studies; the mechanism remains preliminary.
ai_technology: Graph neural network for predicting antibacterial activity

evidence.tested: Bactericidal activity against a wide range of pathogens, including M. tuberculosis and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae; halicin treated C. difficile and pan-resistant A. baumannii infections in mice. Of 23 tested predictions from over 107 million ZINC15 molecules, eight were antibacterial.
evidence.unknown: Human safety and efficacy are not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicted antibacterial activity across chemical libraries; candidates were then tested experimentally.

title: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging battery protocols
summary: A model estimating cycle life from the first 100 cycles, paired with Bayesian optimization, assessed 224 fast-charging protocols in 16 days; the authors estimate exhaustive search without early prediction would take over 500 days. It optimizes protocols, not new materials; only the abstract was reviewed.
organization: Stanford University, MIT, and Toyota Research Institute

title: DSP-1181: an AI-created drug candidate enters Phase I
summary: Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma and Exscientia announced the start in Japan of a Phase I study of DSP-1181, a 5-HT1A serotonin receptor agonist created with the Centaur Chemist platform, with obsessive-compulsive disorder as the first indication. The companies said exploratory research took under 12 months versus a typical 4.5 years. The announcement gives no efficacy results. In the January 31, 2022 investor-call transcript, Sumitomo said development was discontinued because the candidate did not meet the expected Phase I criterion.

title: An AI breast-cancer screening system evaluated in two countries
summary: Among 25,856 women in the UK and 3,097 in the US, the system reduced false positives by 5.7% (US) and 1.2% (UK), and false negatives by 9.4% and 2.7% in absolute terms compared with radiologists. Trained only on UK data, it also outperformed specialists on US data. Retrospective evaluation (Nature): prospective studies are needed, and clinical deployment is unclear.
organization: Google DeepMind, Google Health, Cancer Research UK Imperial Centre, and Northwestern University

title: Delphi-2M forecasts the risk of more than 1,000 diseases
summary: A generative transformer trained on about 0.4 million UK Biobank participants and validated on 1.9 million people in Danish registries predicts rates for more than 1,000 diseases and simulates health trajectories up to 20 years ahead. Reported accuracy is comparable to single-disease models. Retrospective analysis (Nature, abstract read): not a clinical tool and not causal.
organization: DKFZ, EMBL-EBI and University of Copenhagen

title: Serine hydrolases designed from scratch
summary: RFdiffusion backbones and the PLACER network for catalytic-cycle ensembles produced de novo serine hydrolases with kcat/Km up to 4.3e3 M^-1 s^-1 and crystal structures within 1 Å of the designs, in five folds not seen in this enzyme family. Science abstract read; design success rates not checked.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design and UCLA

title: BindCraft designs protein binders in one shot
summary: An open AlphaFold2-based hallucination pipeline designs binders with reported experimental success rates of 10-100% across 12 targets, with affinities predominantly in the nanomolar range. The authors also demonstrated effects in cell assays and patient-derived samples; these are experimental results, not established clinical treatments. This entry uses the Nature publication date (27 August 2025); the preprint appeared in 2024.

title: DrugCLIP screens about 10,000 human proteins against 500 million compounds
summary: Contrastive learning, reported up to 10 million times faster than docking, gave wet-lab hit rates of 15% for the norepinephrine transporter and 17.5% for thyroid hormone receptor interactor 12, with two inhibitor structures solved. Hit rates cover a small set of targets; most of the genome-wide screen is computational. Science abstract read.

title: SMRTnet predicts small molecules that bind RNA
summary: Across 10 disease-associated RNA targets the model yielded 40 hits with nanomolar to micromolar affinity; one compound was tested in three cancer cell lines. A press-release hit rate of 21.1% was not checked against the paper. Nature Biotechnology abstract read.
organization: Tsinghua University, Peking University and China Pharmaceutical University

title: Urania designs new gravitational-wave detectors
summary: An algorithm designing interferometers from scratch produced 50 layouts that, in simulation, raise the potentially observable volume by up to 50-fold (best case). Designs are published as a Detector Zoo. Simulation only: nothing has been built or tested. Phys. Rev. X abstract read.
organization: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light and LIGO Laboratory

title: Erdős Problem #728 solved with GPT-5.2 Pro and Aristotle
summary: GPT-5.2 Pro produced the argument and Harmonic's Aristotle a Lean proof of infinitely many triples with a logarithmic gap in a factorial divisibility condition. The arXiv writeup calls it resolved autonomously, which is the author's claim; no independent review is stated.

title: AlphaEvolve raises nine Ramsey lower bounds
summary: AlphaEvolve-generated search algorithms improved bounds such as R(3,13) from 60 to 61, R(4,16) from 170 to 174 and R(4,19) from 213 to 219. The paper does not describe independent verification; search code is public. arXiv preprint, latest version read.

title: A Herculaneum scroll read end to end without opening
summary: Machine-learning ink detection on synchrotron scans let papyrologists read about 22 columns of a likely Stoic ethics text from scroll PHerc. 1667. The text is fragmentary because only the inner core survives, and humans transcribed and reviewed every reading.
ai_technology: Machine-learning ink detection with virtual unwrapping

title: EVOLVEpro improves proteins up to 100-fold with few experiments
summary: A protein language model combined with a regression model in an active-learning loop improved six proteins used in RNA production, genome editing and antibody binding, with up to 100-fold gains reported in the Science abstract. Online date taken from the November 2024 PubMed record (Europe PMC lists 24 January 2025); per-protein numbers not read.
ai_technology: EVOLVEpro (protein language model with active learning)

title: A closed-loop platform engineers enzymes with minimal human input
summary: Machine learning and language models choosing variants, with a biofoundry running build and test, raised Arabidopsis halide methyltransferase substrate preference 90-fold (16-fold ethyltransferase activity) and Yersinia mollaretii phytase activity 26-fold at neutral pH, in four rounds over four weeks and under 500 variants per enzyme. Two enzymes only; the amount of human setup was not checked in the full text.
ai_technology: Machine learning and LLM-guided variant design with biofoundry automation

title: GPT-4 agents run an end-to-end chemical synthesis workflow
summary: Six GPT-4-based agents (literature, experiment design, hardware, spectra, separation, interpretation) ran a Cu/TEMPO aerobic oxidation workflow with automated hardware and were validated on three further reactions. The abstract gives no yields or timings; full text not read.

title: Gauss formalizes the Strong Prime Number Theorem in Lean
summary: Math Inc's autoformalization agent produced about 25,000 lines of Lean with over 1,000 theorems and definitions in roughly three weeks, on a project set by Terence Tao and Alex Kontorovich in 2024. Figures are company-reported; the project notes targeted human scaffolding and review of key lemmas. Announcement date unconfirmed: September 2025 is taken from the repository's single commit (11 September).

title: PoLARIS: a self-driving microfluidic lab finds brighter lead-free perovskite nanoplatelets
summary: A closed-loop microfluidic platform ran 120 experiments in one 12-hour campaign on double perovskite nanoplatelets with up to six elements and identified the brightest lead-free composition found in that campaign. The press release gives no numerical photoluminescence gain, so the improvement is not quantified in the sources checked. Validation is the authors' own experimental measurements, and the paper should be checked for the brightness figures.
ai_technology: PoLARIS (microfluidic self-driving lab with closed-loop experiment selection)
organization: North Carolina State University; Brown University

title: LFAST: an LLM agent drives robotic synthesis of the new COF-2000 framework
summary: A GPT-4o-based agent (LFAST) screened reaction conditions over a 96-condition matrix and refined them after each round, raising the crystallinity index of a reference covalent organic framework by 350% and yielding COF-2000, a previously unreported material with higher structural order. The reported validation is crystallinity measurement of the synthesized products; the authors do not pursue applications. Publication date is taken from secondary reports of the JACS paper and should be checked against the journal page.
ai_technology: LFAST (LLM For Accelerated Synthesis Technique), GPT-4o agent with robotic experimentation

title: Qiushi Discovery Engine proposes and validates an optical bilinear interaction
summary: An LLM agent (Qiushi Discovery Engine) given only the topic optical computing for AI ran an open-ended study of 145.9 million tokens, 3,242 LLM calls and 1,242 tool calls, and proposed an optical bilinear interaction analogous to the attention operation in Transformers, which the authors say they experimentally validated. The abstract gives no accuracy figure or number of experimental runs. This is an arXiv preprint and the validation is reported by the authors themselves.
ai_technology: Qiushi Discovery Engine (dual-layer LLM agent with Meta-Trace memory)

title: An LLM agent in an air-free robotic lab maps lithium halide spinel conductors
summary: An agent-guided self-driving lab ran 352 air-sensitive synthesis samples, realizing 72% of the 171 pairwise combinations of 19 metals. The share of samples meeting both ionic conductivity above 0.05 mS/cm and high spinel phase purity rose from 1.33% in the first 75 agent-proposed samples to 5.33% in the last 75. This is an arXiv preprint; characterization methods and new-compound counts are not confirmed from the abstract page.
ai_technology: A-Lab GPSS (LLM agent integrated into a robotic synthesis platform)
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and University of California, Berkeley

title: Collaborating LLM agents propose and test a calibration rule for diamond quantum spins
summary: Mutually reviewing LLM agents selected a question about the minimum number of calibration settings needed to predict responses to microwave pulse sequences in diamond spin ensembles, derived the theory and tested it experimentally. The first measurement was inconclusive because of signal drift, and after the protocol was revised the result matched the predictions under unchanged acceptance criteria. The abstract reports no numerical values, and this is an unrefereed arXiv preprint with an authors-reported validation.
ai_technology: Collaborative LLM agents that review each other's work

title: EVE: evolutionary model predicts disease-variant pathogenicity without labels
summary: EVE, an unsupervised deep generative model trained on evolutionary sequence variation across about 140,000 species, predicted pathogenicity for more than 36 million variants in 3,219 disease genes and classified over 256,000 variants of unknown significance. The authors report it outperforms methods trained on labelled disease data and performs on par with high-throughput experimental predictions. Caveat: the authors state EVE is not a diagnostic test.
ai_technology: EVE (deep generative evolutionary model, variational autoencoder)
organization: University of Oxford; Harvard Medical School

title: Akita: predicting 3D genome folding from DNA sequence
summary: Akita, a convolutional network, predicts chromatin contact maps for about 1 Mb of DNA sequence. On held-out data it reaches a Pearson R of 0.61 and Spearman R of 0.56, and it learns an orientation-specific grammar for CTCF binding sites. Caveat: the predictions are computational; the paper applies them to in silico mutagenesis, eQTL interpretation and structural-variant prediction.

title: ColabFold: free protein folding with AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold
summary: ColabFold pairs AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold with fast MMseqs2 homology search, running free on Google Colab. Beyond benchmark comparisons, the paper reports predicting structures for 1,762 Methanocaldococcus jannaschii proteins in 48 hours on one GPU and using predicted complexes to help determine the 120 MDa human nuclear-pore structure with cryo-electron microscopy. The proteome structures are computational predictions, not experimentally validated structures. The nuclear-pore application overlaps the separate nuclear-pore entry; this is a methodological contribution, not an additional independent biological finding.
organization: Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences; Seoul National University

title: Cellpose 2.0: human-in-the-loop training for cell segmentation
summary: Cellpose 2.0 provides pretrained cell-segmentation models that can be fine-tuned with fewer than 1,000 annotated regions of interest, reaching performance close to models trained on up to 200,000 regions. A human-in-the-loop pipeline reduces the required user annotation to about 100 to 200 regions while keeping segmentations high quality. Caveat: the validation is on the authors' benchmark datasets and annotation tests.
ai_technology: Cellpose 2.0 (deep learning cell segmentation, human-in-the-loop fine-tuning)

title: ProtGPT2: a language model generating novel protein sequences
summary: ProtGPT2, a 738-million-parameter autoregressive transformer trained on UniRef50, generates de novo protein sequences in seconds. The authors report the generated sequences are distantly related to natural ones, sample unexplored regions of protein space, and match natural sequences in amino acid and disorder propensities. Caveat: the evaluation is computational (sequence searches and similarity networks), with no experimental validation in the sources checked.
organization: Center for Genomic Regulation, Barcelona; Universitat Pompeu Fabra

title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution with in silico combinatorial screening
summary: A path-independent machine-learning protocol screens full combinatorial protein libraries in silico, with training-set design that avoids near-zero-fitness variants. On a four-site epistatic fitness landscape the optimized protocol reached the global fitness maximum up to 81-fold more often than single-step greedy optimization. Caveat: validation is on a combinatorial fitness landscape dataset, not a new wet-lab evolution campaign.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-assisted directed evolution (in silico combinatorial screening)

title: Cell2location: mapping fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomics
summary: Cell2location is a Bayesian model that resolves fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomics data by accounting for technical variation and sharing information across locations. Applied to three tissues, it revealed regional astrocyte subtypes in mouse brain, a rare pre-germinal center B cell population in human lymph node, and fine immune populations in human gut lymphoid follicles. Caveat: the reported results are biological findings from the method's application, with no single quantitative accuracy figure confirmed in the abstract.

title: Archaeasins: deep learning finds antibiotic candidates in the archaeal proteome
summary: The APEX 1.1 deep learning platform scanned 233 archaeal proteomes and flagged 12,623 candidate antimicrobial molecules. Of 80 synthesized candidates, 93% showed in vitro activity against key pathogens, and three selected compounds reduced a drug-resistant bacterium in animal models after a single dose. Candidate and synthesis counts differ between press coverage and secondary reports, and the mouse details come from press coverage rather than the full text, so the paper's own figures should be checked.
ai_technology: APEX 1.1 deep learning antimicrobial peptide predictor
organization: University of Pennsylvania (de la Fuente lab)

title: ModelAngelo: automated atomic model building in cryo-EM maps
summary: A single graph neural network combining cryo-EM map density, protein sequence and local geometry builds protein models that the authors report are of similar quality to those built by human experts. Its sequence identification, using predicted amino acid probabilities in hidden Markov model searches, outperformed human experts on proteins of unknown sequence. Evidence is benchmark-based on the authors' own comparisons, with no new biological finding reported.
ai_technology: ModelAngelo graph neural network with hidden Markov model sequence search
organization: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (Scheres group)

title: RFdiffusion2 scaffolds enzyme active sites at atomic level
summary: RFdiffusion2 scaffolded all 41 active sites in a diverse benchmark, compared with 16 for previous methods. Designs were tested experimentally, with fewer than 96 sequences needed per case to find active enzymes across three catalytic mechanisms. The journal abstract's three-mechanism count conflicts with a five-reaction claim in the Institute for Protein Design announcement, so the abstract should be treated as authoritative.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design (Baker lab)

title: Computational design of zinc metallohydrolases with RFdiffusion2
summary: RFdiffusion2 designed zinc metallohydrolases from quantum-chemistry-derived active-site geometries. The first round of 96 designs produced an enzyme with catalytic efficiency of 16,000 M-1 s-1, and a second round of 96 yielded three more highly active enzymes, with k/K up to 53,000 M-1 s-1. Crystal structures (PDB 9PYJ, 9PYL) were determined, but the evidence covers one designed enzyme family.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design (Baker lab)

evidence.tested: From 96 designs, the best had kcat/KM of 16,000 M^-1 s^-1; a second round of 96 gave three more active enzymes, up to 53,000 M^-1 s^-1 and kcat up to 1.5 s^-1. The crystal structure of the most active design is very close to the model.
evidence.unknown: Use in practical applications is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion2 designed zinc metallohydrolases from quantum-chemistry active sites; PLACER and Chai-1 analysed the designs.

title: Riff-Diff: computational enzyme design by catalytic motif scaffolding
summary: Riff-Diff places catalytic motifs around an active centre and uses RFdiffusion to generate the full protein; 35 tested sequences yielded active enzymes for several reaction types, reported as significantly faster than earlier computational designs. Angstrom-level accuracy was checked against experimentally determined high-resolution structures, and almost all designs kept their fold up to about 90 degrees Celsius. Figures come from university press coverage; the Nature paper itself was not read directly.
organization: TU Graz and University of Graz (Oberdorfer group)

title: A designed generalist binding protein evolves into a highly active designed enzyme
summary: Crystallographic fragment screening found weak binders of a designed protein, which were then evolved into a catalyst that the authors describe as the most active designed enzyme to date. AI models were used in the redesign step, while the crystal structures and enzyme assays were experimental. Kinetic values and design counts were not checked in the primary paper, so the record claim rests on press statements.
ai_technology: AI-guided protein redesign (specific models not verified)
organization: University of California, San Francisco (Fraser and DeGrado groups)

title: Self-driving laboratory optimizes organic hole-transport thin films
summary: A closed-loop robotic platform autonomously varied film composition and processing to maximize the hole mobility of organic hole-transport materials for perovskite solar cells. The optimization was demonstrated experimentally on the robot, and the paper is peer-reviewed in Science Advances. Numeric mobility gains were not verified, so the size of the improvement is unconfirmed.
ai_technology: Closed-loop self-driving laboratory with autonomous optimization
organization: University of British Columbia; Harvard University; University of Toronto

title: Generative AI and on-chip synthesis produce new LXR agonists
summary: A recurrent neural network generated de novo LXR agonist designs, and 25 were synthesized in a microfluidic flow system. In vitro screening found 17 hits (68%), and 12 were confirmed as potent LXR agonists after batch resynthesis. Validation is in vitro only, with no in vivo testing, and the sources disagree on the number of designs retained for synthesis.
ai_technology: LSTM recurrent neural network generator with transfer learning, coupled to on-chip flow synthesis

title: Machine learning and experiments yield tolerant polymer dielectrics
summary: An informatics screen of over 13,000 known polymers, combined with phenomenological models, selected representative dielectric candidates for experimental testing. Two of the proposed polymers were synthesized and reported as tolerant to field and temperature extremes. The validation set is very small, and the exact property values were not verified in this search.
ai_technology: Machine learning and informatics models for polymer dielectric screening

title: Unsupervised machine learning guides discovery of a lithium solid electrolyte
summary: Unsupervised machine learning of experimentally explored chemistry, combined with crystal structure prediction, selected element combinations for new inorganic solids. The approach predicted a novel quaternary lithium solid electrolyte that was then synthesized, and the group reports four new materials in total. The conductivity values of the synthesized compounds were not verified in this search.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine learning for element selection with crystal structure prediction

title: Machine learning and DFT discover high-entropy Invar alloys
summary: A closed-loop active-learning framework combining machine learning, density-functional theory and thermodynamic calculations screened millions of compositions. Of 17 new alloys processed and characterized, two high-entropy Invar alloys showed very low thermal expansion, about 2 x 10^-6 per kelvin at 300 K. Only the top-ranked candidates were synthesized, so the hit rate is small.
ai_technology: Closed-loop active learning combining machine learning, density-functional theory and thermodynamic calculations
organization: Max Planck Institute for Iron Research; Delft University of Technology

title: Catalysis AI Agent derives design rules for copper single-atom alloys for CO2 electroreduction
summary: An LLM-based Catalysis AI Agent identified an energy descriptor for classifying copper-based single-atom alloys and a structural descriptor for predicting activation energy. The team reports experimental testing and that the approach extends to other metal dopants. Evidence caveat: the press release gives no quantitative activity or selectivity values and does not name the experimental group, so validation is limited.
organization: Tohoku University, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR)

title: ChatHEA assistant guides high-entropy alloy catalysts for fuel cells
summary: ChatHEA, a domain-specific LLM assistant for high-entropy alloy electrocatalysis, guided synthesis and screening of 100 five-element alloy catalysts. The FeCoCuPtIr catalyst reached a peak power density of 0.789 W cm-2 in a fuel cell and outperformed commercial Pt/C in electrochemical tests. These figures are reported by the institutional press release; its numeric activity values and DOE target are not given. The catalog date is the paper's 14 March 2026 publication date, stated in the 8 July press release; the full paper was not reviewed.
organization: Tohoku University, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR)

title: Deep learning finds multimetallic single-atom catalysts across material families
summary: The Crossbreeding Neural Network (CBNN), trained jointly on carbon-supported single-atom catalysts and perovskite oxides, screened 8,008 candidates. Its top W-Mo-Ru-Rh design on a perovskite support outperformed the comparison catalysts in electrochemical tests, and the activity ranking of 12 tested catalysts matched the predictions. These counts come from the IBS institutional release; the paper abstract confirms the experimental result but does not quantify the activity gain. The catalog date is the Nature Materials publication date, 28 May 2026.
organization: Institute for Basic Science (IBS) Center for Nanoparticle Research; Seoul National University

title: Machine learning pre-screening finds kagome superconductors YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2
summary: A machine-learning pre-screen of candidate compounds, followed by first-principles calculations, selected YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, which were measured as bulk superconductors with Tc of 0.81 K and 0.95 K and near 100% superconducting volume fraction. Evidence caveat: these are low-temperature superconductors and the work is a proof-of-concept screening workflow, not a room-temperature result; LuRu3B2 was initially overlooked because of a phonon instability.
ai_technology: Machine-learning pre-screening combined with first-principles calculations
organization: Aalto University; Rice University; Princeton University

title: MOFGen: agentic AI generates MOF linkers and five AI-designed MOFs are synthesized
summary: MOFGen, a multi-agent system combining language models, diffusion models and quantum-mechanical checks, generated hundreds of thousands of novel MOF structures and synthesizable linkers. The authors report that five AI-designed MOFs were synthesized through high-throughput experiments. Evidence caveat: the abstract describes the validation only generally, the structure counts are computational, and this is an arXiv preprint not confirmed as peer-reviewed.
ai_technology: MOFGen (multi-agent LLM system with diffusion model)
organization: UC Berkeley; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; Google DeepMind

title: Canopy traits across tropical forests mapped with deep learning and satellite data
summary: Field data from more than 1,800 vegetation plots, combined with satellite, terrain, climate and soil data and convolutional neural networks, predicted variation in 13 tree functional traits. Tropical American forests show about 40% greater functional richness than African and Asian forests, and African forests show 32% higher functional divergence than American forests. The authors caution that accuracy depends on data quality and coverage, and that AI should support rather than replace field sampling.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural networks combined with satellite spectral data

title: WenHai: a deep neural network forecasts the eddying ocean
summary: The WenHai data-driven global ocean forecast system outperforms a state-of-the-art eddy-resolving numerical model and an AI-based ocean forecast system for temperature and salinity profiles, sea surface temperature, sea level anomaly and near-surface currents at lead times from 1 day to at least 10 days. Skill beyond 10 days is not reported in the abstract, and the computational speed-up claimed in secondary coverage was not confirmed in the paper abstract.
ai_technology: WenHai deep neural network ocean forecasting model
organization: Laoshan Laboratory; Ocean University of China

title: Samudra: an AI emulator of the global ocean for climate simulations
summary: Samudra, a UNet-style emulator trained on the ocean component of a state-of-the-art climate model (OM4 within CM4), reproduces sea surface height, velocities, temperature and salinity across the full ocean depth. It runs about 150 times faster than the original ocean model and remains stable for centuries. The authors note it struggles to reproduce the correct magnitude of forcing trends while staying stable, so it needs further work.
organization: Princeton University and NOAA Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory

title: Deep learning forecasts aftershock rates in seconds, comparable to ETAS
summary: Neural networks trained on earthquake catalogues from California, New Zealand, Italy, Japan and Greece forecast the number of aftershocks in the following 24 hours after magnitude 4+ earthquakes. Their quality is reported as comparable to the operational ETAS model, while producing results in seconds rather than hours or days. The abstract reports no numeric skill scores, so the comparison rests on the full paper.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks for spatiotemporal seismicity rate forecasting, benchmarked against ETAS
organization: University of Edinburgh, British Geological Survey and University of Padua

title: Deep transfer learning detects methane super-emitters in oil and gas fields from Sentinel-2
summary: A two-part framework (adaptive artifact removal plus a deep subdomain adaptation network) was trained on 1,627 Sentinel-2 images from six known methane super-emitters. Applied to an unannotated oil field in Algeria, it flagged 34 anomalous emission events over one year, attributed to three super-emitters linked to production and transmission infrastructure. DSAN achieved an average macro F1 of 0.86 on transfer tasks, versus 0.78 for the EfficientNet-V2L comparator; independent field verification is not reported in the abstract.
ai_technology: Deep subdomain adaptation network (DSAN) with low-reflectance artifact detection (LRAD)
organization: Westlake University; Zhejiang University; Harvard University

title: De novo designed proteins modulate GPCR signalling in the dopamine D1 receptor
summary: Zhejiang University designed four de novo GPCR exoframe modulators (GEMs) that target the transmembrane domain of the dopamine D1 receptor. Functional assays showed they act as positive, negative or biased allosteric modulators, and one restored activity in loss-of-function receptor mutants. Design is computational; the exact assay numbers were not checked against the full paper, so use the paper for quantitative claims.
ai_technology: Computational de novo protein design (AI-based protein design pipeline)

title: AI-designed protein family binds and senses small molecules, including cortisol
summary: Designed binding proteins for six small-molecule classes, built on a deep-learning NTF2-like fold, were experimentally characterised; one was turned into a cortisol biosensor. Sensitivity reported earlier as nanomolar in the 2023 preprint; the 2026 peer-reviewed version is the source of record. Affinity and sensor figures were not re-checked against the full text.
ai_technology: Deep learning protein design (RFdiffusion-style backbone design with NTF2-like scaffold)
organization: KAIST; University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

title: Adaptive AI experiment planning finds multi-promoter catalysts in under 50 experiments
summary: Fritz Haber Institute, with BASF and BasCat, used adaptive experiment planning in a self-driving lab to search over 10^13 promoter combinations with fewer than 50 experiments. The method was validated on propane-to-propylene conversion, and the authors report synergistic promoter effects that explain the catalyst's performance. The claim of outperforming the industry reference is not quantified in the release, so check the paper for numbers.
ai_technology: Adaptive experiment planning (Bayesian-style, gray-box) in a self-driving lab
organization: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society; BASF; BasCat (UniCat BASF JointLab)

title: Machine learning designs bulk metallic glasses with about 2,450 HV hardness
summary: Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials used VIBANN, an attention-based variational network trained on only 673 compositions, to design hard multicomponent bulk metallic glasses. Five alloys were synthesised as fully amorphous 2 mm rods, reaching about 2,450 HV, with high-energy X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics explaining the origin. The abstract gives inconsistent hardness values (about 2,450 vs above 2,050 HV), so verify the figure in the paper.
organization: Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials

title: AI designs physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups
summary: Krenn group (Tübingen, TU Wien and collaborators) treats experiment design as an optimisation problem, using physics simulations to propose and refine setups that yield more precise measurements than human designs across several physics areas. The institutional announcements give no quantitative figures, so the claim rests on the Nature paper, which should be read for the numbers. Evidence strength is therefore unverified from press material alone.
ai_technology: AI-driven optimisation of experimental setups (Krenn group method, simulation-based search)
organization: University of Tübingen; TU Wien; University of Vienna

title: PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI
summary: PatternBoost alternates a local search that generates candidate constructions with a transformer trained on the best ones. The authors report the best known solutions to several extremal combinatorics problems, including a counterexample to a conjecture that had been open for 30 years. Candidates are scored mechanically, so each construction is checked by computer; the abstract does not name the conjecture and the paper was not peer-reviewed at the time of posting.
ai_technology: PatternBoost (transformer trained on search outputs, combined with local search)
organization: Meta AI; University of Wisconsin-Madison; Google DeepMind; University of Sydney

title: Barbarians at the Gate: AI-driven research for systems (ADRS)
summary: An LLM-driven generate-evaluate-refine loop built on OpenEvolve produced systems algorithms in case studies, with the abstract reporting up to 5.0x runtime improvements or 50% cost reductions over baselines. Solutions are checked with simulators or real systems, which is the validation basis. The results are on specific case studies rather than a general claim, and the work is a preprint.
ai_technology: OpenEvolve (LLM-driven evolutionary code search, ADRS framework)

title: Gauss completes the Lean formalization of the dimension-8 sphere packing proof
summary: Math Inc's autoformalization model Gauss completed the final stages of the Lean verification of Viazovska's proof that the E8 lattice is the optimal sphere packing in dimension 8, working with the human formalization team. The paper describes the human-AI collaboration and the verification in the Lean kernel, with the milestone dated February 2026 in the abstract. Formalization of an existing 2016 result, not a new theorem, and the paper is a progress report.
ai_technology: Gauss (Math Inc autoformalization model) with Lean
organization: Math Inc; Hariharan, Viazovska and collaborators

title: AI-driven formal proof search resolves Erdős problems and OEIS conjectures
summary: An agent that alternates LLM proof generation with Lean verification autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures, at a cost of a few hundred dollars per problem according to the abstract. Proofs are Lean-verified, so the checking is mechanical; the abstract does not name the system and the results are limited to the problem sets tested.
ai_technology: LLM-based agent with Lean-based proof verification (system unnamed in abstract)

title: AMIE: conversational diagnostic AI rated above primary care physicians in simulated consultations
summary: In a blinded remote OSCE with 149 case scenarios, AMIE and primary care physicians held text consultations with simulated patients. Specialist physicians rated AMIE superior on 30 of 32 axes and patient actors on 25 of 26, and non-inferior on the rest. The evidence comes from simulated scenarios, not real patients, and the authors state that further research is needed before real-world use.
ai_technology: AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), a large language model agent for diagnostic dialogue

title: COMPOSER deep learning sepsis model linked to 17% lower in-hospital sepsis mortality
summary: Across two UC San Diego Health emergency departments, 6,217 adult septic patients were studied before and after nurse-facing alerts driven by the COMPOSER model. Deployment was associated with a 1.9-point absolute (17% relative) drop in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI 0.3-3.5%) and a 5-point rise in bundle compliance. The design is quasi-experimental, not randomized, and several authors co-founded a company that commercializes the tools.
organization: UC San Diego Health; University of California San Diego

title: RETFound: a foundation model for disease detection from retinal images
summary: RETFound is self-pretrained on unlabelled retinal images, reportedly about 1.6 million from Moorfields Eye Hospital, and then adapted to disease tasks. The authors report better diagnosis of sight-threatening eye diseases than comparison models, better prediction of systemic conditions such as heart failure and myocardial infarction, and strong performance with fewer labels. The evaluation is retrospective, with no clinical deployment study, and the model was released openly.
ai_technology: RETFound (masked-autoencoder foundation model for retinal images)
organization: Moorfields Eye Hospital; University College London

title: PANDA: pancreatic lesion detection on non-contrast CT with deep learning
summary: PANDA was trained on non-contrast abdominal CT scans from 3,208 patients at a high-volume pancreatic cancer centre in Shanghai. On a separate chest CT test set it reported 86.0% sensitivity and 98.9% specificity for lesion detection. The evidence is retrospective, and the press figure of 93% sensitivity on a larger set of over 20,000 scans is not confirmed against the primary paper.
ai_technology: PANDA (three-stage deep learning cascade on non-contrast CT)
organization: DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Shanghai Institute of Pancreatic Diseases; First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University

title: Prov-GigaPath: a whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology
summary: Pretrained on 1.3 billion image tiles from 171,189 whole-slide images of more than 30,000 patients across 31 tissue types, Prov-GigaPath achieved state-of-the-art results on 25 of 26 evaluated tasks. Validation uses retrospective data from a single US health network, and the model weights were released openly.
ai_technology: Prov-GigaPath (GigaPath vision transformer with LongNet dilated attention)
organization: Microsoft Research; Providence; University of Washington

title: Virchow: a pathology foundation model for clinical-grade cancer detection
summary: Virchow was trained on about 1.5 million H&E whole-slide images from roughly 100,000 patients at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. Its pan-cancer detector reached a 0.95 specimen-level AUC and matched or exceeded tissue-specific clinical-grade models on some rare cancers. Evaluation is retrospective, and the study is co-authored by the company Paige, whose press materials carry the headline claims.
ai_technology: Virchow (vision transformer foundation model for pathology)
organization: Paige; Microsoft Research; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

title: PI-CAI: AI matches or beats radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI
summary: In a reader study with 62 radiologists on 400 cases, the AI detected about 6.8% more clinically significant cancers at the same specificity and produced about 50% fewer false positives. On 1,000 routine-practice cases, however, non-inferiority was not confirmed (specificity 68.9% vs 69.0% at 96.1% sensitivity). The authors call for prospective validation, and the system is not available for clinical use.
ai_technology: PI-CAI challenge super-algorithm (ensemble of top five submitted deep learning models)
organization: PI-CAI consortium; Radboud University Medical Center

title: EchoNext: detecting structural heart disease from ECGs with AI
summary: EchoNext was trained on more than 1 million paired heart-rhythm and imaging records from a large health system and outperformed cardiologists in a controlled evaluation. In a prospective clinical trial of patients without prior cardiac imaging, it identified previously undiagnosed heart disease. Exact performance figures were not verified in this search, and model weights and an annotated dataset were released publicly.

evidence.tested: Trained on over 1 million rhythm and imaging records; high accuracy in internal and external validation; outperformed cardiologists in a controlled evaluation; prospectively evaluated in a clinical trial of patients without previous cardiac imaging, identifying undiagnosed disease.
evidence.unknown: Effect on outcomes or costs of screening is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: EchoNext, a deep learning model reading electrocardiograms; weights and an annotated dataset were released.

title: Conversations with an AI chatbot durably reduce conspiracy beliefs
