summary: Across experiments with more than 2,000 participants, three dialogues with GPT-4 reduced belief in the targeted conspiracy theory by about 20%, and the effect persisted for two months and spilled over to unrelated conspiracies. A professional fact-checker rated 99.2% of 128 sampled chatbot claims as true. Caveats: lab setting, the chatbot did not reduce belief in true conspiracies, and most participants still held the hoax belief.
organization: MIT Sloan School of Management; Cornell University; American University

title: Instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis for a man with ALS
summary: A brain-computer interface decoding 256 microelectrodes in the ventral precentral gyrus synthesized the participant's intended voice causally, with a reported latency of about 10 ms per decoding step. Listeners understood almost 60% of synthesized words, compared with 4% when he was not using the device, and he could modulate intonation and sing short melodies. Caveat: a single participant with ALS, within the BrainGate2 trial, and the authors describe the technology as early stage.
ai_technology: Deep neural network speech decoder for intracortical recordings
organization: UC Davis; Stanford University; BrainGate consortium

title: Centaur: a foundation model that predicts human behaviour across psychology experiments
summary: Fine-tuning Llama 3.1 70B on Psych-101, a dataset of about 10 million human choices from 160 psychology experiments, produced a model that predicts and simulates human behaviour in experiments expressed in natural language, including tasks it had not seen. The authors report that its internal representations align better with human neural activity after fine-tuning. Caveat: a 2025 critique argues that its language comprehension is limited and that it fails to follow altered instructions.
organization: Helmholtz Munich; Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics; University of Tübingen

title: Generative agents built from interview transcripts simulate 1,000 people
summary: LLM agents built from participants' full interview transcripts reproduced their General Social Survey answers at about 85% of the rate at which participants reproduced their own answers two weeks later, a normalized score. They also matched personality and economic-game results (normalized correlations of about 0.80 and 0.66) and replicated four of five behavioural experiments. Caveat: arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, and the results are normalized rather than raw accuracy.
ai_technology: Generative agent architecture with LLM and full interview transcripts
organization: Stanford University; Google DeepMind; Northwestern University; University of Washington

title: Deep learning maps Angkorian-period reservoirs beyond Greater Angkor
summary: A DeepLabV3+ segmentation model trained on about 3,600 high-quality samples from over 11,000 candidates mapped Angkor-period reservoirs in satellite imagery across the wider Angkorian realm. The best F1 score reached 45% in favourable regions, comparable to a trained human interpreter. The authors present the model as a second opinion for landscape archaeologists that requires human validation.
organization: Leiden University; University of Toronto; University of Colorado Boulder

title: Mind captioning: text descriptions of viewed videos decoded from fMRI
summary: A language-model pipeline mapped fMRI activity from six participants to semantic signatures of 2,180 captioned videos and generated text matching them. The generated descriptions identified the correct video among 100 candidates about 50% of the time, against a chance level of about 1%, and the method worked for recalled clips and without the brain's language areas. Caveats: small participant group, needs extensive per-person data and cooperative subjects, and the authors note it cannot read private thoughts.
ai_technology: Deep language model semantic-feature decoder with text generation search

evidence.tested: Descriptions generated from brain activity induced by videos captured the viewed content and generalized to recalled content, even without relying on the canonical language network.
evidence.unknown: Use with people who have aphasia is described as a potential, not tested in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: Linear decoders map brain activity to semantic features from a deep language model; candidate text is optimized to match them.

title: The levers of political persuasion with conversational AI
summary: In three large experiments with 76,977 participants, 19 LLMs argued 707 British political positions in dialogue. Persuasiveness was driven mainly by information density, while tailoring to user traits added little, and post-training for persuasion raised effectiveness by up to 50%. The most persuasive models also produced the most inaccurate claims. Caveat: the persuasion effects are measured in survey experiments, and accuracy was tested on a subset of claims.
ai_technology: 19 open and closed LLMs (including GPT-4.5, GPT-4o, Grok-3)
organization: University of Oxford; UK AI Security Institute; London School of Economics; Stanford University; MIT

title: RAVEN pipeline validates 118 new TESS planets and vets over 2,000 candidates
summary: A pipeline combining box least squares detection with machine-learning classifiers, trained on realistic simulations, searched 2.2 million TESS main-sequence stars in full-frame images (sectors 1 to 55). It newly validates 118 planets, 31 of them newly detected, and vets over 2,000 candidates, about 1,000 of them new. The machine-learning classifier is a validation tool rather than the detection method, and the paper is a preprint accepted for MNRAS; the peer-reviewed publication date was not confirmed.
ai_technology: RAVEN: box least squares detection with machine-learning vetting classifiers trained on simulations

title: Physics-tailored machine learning reveals unexpected non-reciprocal forces in dusty plasmas
summary: A neural network built with physical constraints was trained on 3D particle-tracking data from a laboratory dusty plasma to infer the interaction forces between particles. The method describes the non-reciprocal forces more precisely than before and shows that some common theoretical assumptions about them are inaccurate. The authors checked their inferred force laws against laboratory experiments, which strengthens the claim, though the result comes from a single experimental system.
ai_technology: Physics-tailored neural network for inferring force laws from particle trajectories

title: Machine-learning alert flags supernova 2023zkd as a black hole and star binary merger
summary: The LAISS machine-learning alert system flagged the transient SN 2023zkd months before its most unusual behaviour, and the team then analysed its four-year optical precursor. The authors conclude that a massive, partly stripped helium star merged with a black hole companion, with the second light peak explained by a collision with a dense disk-like cloud. The ML step only prioritised the event; the physical interpretation is model-based, and outlets give conflicting accounts of who first detected it.
ai_technology: LAISS machine-learning anomaly alert for transient detection
organization: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian; MIT; University of California Santa Cruz; Young Supernova Experiment

title: First-principles neural network finds crystallization of fractional quantum Hall liquids
summary: A self-attention neural-network wavefunction (MagNet), trained only by minimising the microscopic Hamiltonian of interacting electrons in a magnetic field, finds both topological liquid and electron-crystal ground states across a range of Landau-level mixing. The authors present it as a method that discovers correlated phases without assumptions. This is an arXiv preprint with computational results only, not yet checked experimentally or peer reviewed.

title: Deep-learning CADe colonoscopy raises adenoma detection in a double-blind trial
summary: In a double-blind randomised trial of 962 patients in China (484 analysed with CADe, 478 with a sham system), the deep-learning system raised adenoma detection to 34% (165/484) from 28% (132/478), OR 1.36 (95% CI 1.03-1.79). The primary analysis was per protocol, the trial was single-centre, and the abstract reports no ITT analysis.
ai_technology: Deep-learning computer-aided detection (CADe) system for polyps during colonoscopy
organization: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center

title: COMPOSER sepsis model flags unfamiliar cases instead of guessing
summary: COMPOSER, a deep-learning early sepsis predictor, reached AUCs of 0.925-0.953 in ICU and 0.938-0.945 in ED across six cohorts (515,720 patients) from two US health systems. About 20% of non-septic and 8% of septic prediction windows were marked indeterminate, and the model gave a median early warning of 12.2 hours in ICU and 2.1 hours in ED before the first antibiotics order. The abstract reports no prospective deployment or patient-outcome results.
ai_technology: COMPOSER deep-learning model with uncertainty-based indeterminate output

title: Combining AI algorithms with radiologists improves mammography specificity
summary: An international crowdsourced challenge (over 1,100 participants, 126 teams, 44 countries) tested AI on screening mammograms from 144,231 US and 166,578 Swedish examinations. The best single algorithm did not beat radiologists (US AUC 0.858), but an ensemble of top algorithms combined with US radiologists' recall decisions reached AUC 0.942 and 92.0% specificity at the same sensitivity. The study is retrospective, uses challenge data and does not report recall rates.
ai_technology: Ensemble of crowdsourced deep-learning mammography algorithms combined with radiologist recall
organization: Sage Bionetworks and DREAM challenge collaborators, with US and Swedish screening programmes

title: Deep learning detects pancreatic cancer on CT in a nationwide study
summary: A deep-learning tool for contrast-enhanced CT reached 89.9% sensitivity and 95.9% specificity in an internal test set (not significantly different from the original radiologist reports, 96.1%). On 1,473 real-world Taiwanese CT studies it reached 89.7% sensitivity and 92.8% specificity, but sensitivity for cancers under 2 cm was 74.7%. The study is retrospective, with no prospective reader comparison in the abstract.
ai_technology: Segmentation CNN with an ensemble of five CNN classifiers for pancreatic cancer on CT
organization: National Taiwan University Hospital; National Taiwan University

title: CNN distinguishes pancreatic cancer on contrast CT with cross-racial validation
summary: A CNN trained on contrast-enhanced CT from a Taiwanese centre reached 98.3% sensitivity on combined local test sets versus 92.9% for radiologists (difference 5.4 points, p=0.014). On a US external test set, sensitivity fell to 79.0% with specificity 97.6% (AUC 0.920), and sensitivity for tumours under 2 cm was 63.1% in that set. The study is retrospective and the authors describe it as supplementary to radiologists.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network applied to CT image patches
organization: National Taiwan University; National Taiwan University Hospital

title: Med-BERT pretrained on structured health records improves disease prediction
summary: Med-BERT, a transformer pretrained on structured EHR data from 28,490,650 patients, improved AUC by 1.21% to 6.14% across two disease-prediction tasks compared with prior baselines. The gains are reported on retrospective structured-data tasks, and the abstract gives no clinical deployment or outcome results.
ai_technology: Med-BERT, BERT-style transformer pretrained on structured electronic health records
organization: University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

title: Self-reported symptom app predicts likely COVID-19 infection in real time
summary: A COVID Symptom Study app with 2,618,862 participants and 18,401 tested users found loss of smell or taste in 65.03% of positives versus 21.71% of negatives (OR 6.74). A machine-learning model applied to 805,753 users predicted 140,312 (17.42%) as likely infected. The inputs are self-reported and the test-verified subset is small relative to the user base, so the prediction is not a clinical diagnosis.
ai_technology: Machine-learning symptom model on self-reported app data
organization: King's College London; Massachusetts General Hospital

title: COVNet deep learning separates COVID-19 from other pneumonia on chest CT
summary: The COVNet 3D deep-learning model, trained on 4,352 CT scans from 3,322 patients, reached per-scan sensitivity 90% and specificity 96% (AUC 0.96) for COVID-19, and AUC 0.95 for community-acquired pneumonia. The study is retrospective and evaluated on Chinese cohorts, so performance in other populations is not established.
ai_technology: COVNet, a 3D convolutional neural network on chest CT
organization: Wuhan Huangpi People's Hospital; Wuhan Pulmonary Hospital; Liaocheng People's Hospital

title: AI augmentation lifts radiologists in telling COVID-19 from other pneumonia
summary: A CT model trained on 1,186 patients (521 COVID-19, 665 other pneumonia) reached 95% sensitivity and 96% specificity internally, and AUC 0.90 on an independent test set. Radiologist accuracy rose from 85% to 90% with AI assistance. The study is retrospective and the independent-test performance is lower than the internal result.
ai_technology: Deep-learning CT classifier used as an assistant for radiologists
organization: Xiangya Hospital, Central South University; Rhode Island Hospital; University of Pennsylvania

title: PENet detects pulmonary embolism on volumetric CT angiography
summary: PENet, a 3D deep-learning model for pulmonary embolism on CT angiography, reached AUROC 0.84 on an internal hold-out test and 0.85 on data from one unnamed external institution. The abstract does not report sensitivity, specificity or study size, and the external validation is limited to a single site.
ai_technology: PENet, 3D deep convolutional network on volumetric CT

title: Deep neural networks diagnose brain tumours in minutes from stimulated Raman histology
summary: CNNs trained on over 2.5 million stimulated Raman histology images produced intraoperative brain tumour diagnoses in under 150 seconds, with 94.6% accuracy versus 93.9% for pathologists. The accuracy comparison comes from a prospective multicentre trial with 278 patients, but the abstract does not report sensitivity or specificity separately.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks on stimulated Raman histology images
organization: University of Michigan; Columbia University; University of Miami

evidence.tested: Multicenter prospective clinical trial (n = 278): CNN diagnosis of stimulated Raman images was non-inferior to pathologists reading conventional histology (94.6% versus 93.9%), in under 150 seconds.
evidence.unknown: Long-term patient outcomes are not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: Convolutional neural networks trained on over 2.5 million stimulated Raman histology images.

title: Fusing CT images and EHR data with deep learning improves pulmonary embolism detection
summary: A deep multimodal network combining CT imaging with electronic health record data reached AUROC 0.947 (95% CI 0.946-0.948) on a held-out test set for pulmonary embolism. The abstract reports no sensitivity, specificity, study size or external validation sites, so the evidence is limited to retrospective internal testing.
ai_technology: Multimodal deep neural network fusing CT and EHR data

title: Satellite model maps collapse and surviving Acropora corals in Belize
summary: A supervised Random Tree classifier on satellite images predicted a drop of over 90% in live Acropora cover at Belize from 2011 to 2023 across 25 km². Field searches in June 2025 found live or recently dead colonies at 28 of 42 predicted sites and live colonies at 16 previously undocumented locations. The field check was a search for survivors at sites the model flagged, not a blind test.
ai_technology: Random Tree supervised classification of satellite imagery (machine learning)
organization: Washington and Lee University; Macalester College

title: YOLO detector tracks endangered European hamster activity in camera traps
summary: A YOLO object-detection model trained on 2023 camera-trap videos detected European hamsters with an F1-score of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.93. Its activity profile matched human annotation and showed peak activity at dusk and a secondary peak before sunrise. The evidence covers one season at one monitoring setup, so generalization to other sites is untested.

title: BirdNET embeddings distinguish individual North Atlantic right whales
summary: Audio embeddings from the BirdNET model robustly distinguished individual North Atlantic right whales in upcall recordings from 234 samples across 11 individuals at 3 sites. Simulations showed that an extra 7 dB or more of signal excess is needed to identify individuals under ambient noise. The study uses on-animal archival tags on an endangered species, but the sample is small and the model was not trained for whales.
organization: Cornell K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics; Oregon State University; Syracuse University

title: FluEmbed predicts H3N2 antigenic drift from sequence alone
summary: FluEmbed, a protein language model framework, predicted influenza A (H3N2) antigenicity from RNA sequence with Spearman correlations of 0.67 to 0.80 against hemagglutination inhibition titers. It outperformed Hamming, BLOSUM62 and phylogenetic baselines, and in-silico mutagenesis showed unconstrained mutations carry greater escape potential outside dominant lineages. Validation uses existing HI assay data and retrospective sequences; no new wet-lab tests were run.

title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies palladium catalysts that form dinuclear complexes
summary: A workflow built on only five experimental data points screened 348 phosphine ligands and predicted ligands that favour dinuclear Pd(I) complexes over Pd(0) and Pd(II) species. The authors experimentally verified the predictions, including ligands that had never been synthesized before. The evidence is limited to the Pd speciation system studied, not a general catalyst performance gain.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine learning workflow with clustering on generalized parameter databases and in silico data
organization: RWTH Aachen University; University of Jyväskylä

title: Autonomous robotic system maps Bi2O3 synthesis phase diagram with active learning
summary: The SARA agent combined robotic laser spike annealing, optical characterization and nested active learning to map synthesis phase boundaries of Bi2O3. It reached orders-of-magnitude faster establishment of the phase diagram and identified conditions that stabilize metastable delta-Bi2O3. Validation is experimental but restricted to one oxide system.
ai_technology: Scientific Autonomous Reasoning Agent (SARA) with hierarchical active learning and uncertainty quantification
organization: Cornell University; University of Bern; California Institute of Technology

title: Retrosynthetic software finds experimentally validated supply routes for umifenovir
summary: Retrosynthesis software proposed alternative chemical supply routes for the antiviral umifenovir and eleven other antiviral and anti-inflammatory drugs. The authors experimentally validated four routes to umifenovir and one route to bromhexine, one of which converts six C-H bonds. The work is a proof of route feasibility for supply-chain resilience, not a new therapeutic claim.
ai_technology: Computer-aided retrosynthesis software with exclusion of known starting materials
organization: University of Michigan; MilliporeSigma; Entos, Inc.

title: Machine-learned design of CuPd nanocubes for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia
summary: Interpretable machine learning identified ordered B2 CuPd intermetallics whose adsorption energies break the usual scaling relations. The team synthesized monodisperse CuPd nanocubes that reached a 92.5% Faradaic efficiency at -0.5 V RHE for nitrate reduction to ammonia, with a yield of 6.25 mol h-1 g-1 at -0.6 V. Performance was measured in the authors' own electrochemical tests, and the design rules come from a limited set of predicted intermetallics.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine learning on d-state Pauli repulsion descriptors (DFT-based)
organization: Virginia Tech; National University of Singapore; Argonne National Laboratory

title: Earth-abundant Ni3Mo alloy outperforms platinum for ethane dehydrogenation
summary: A microkinetic and high-throughput screen of 1,998 bimetallic alloys, combined with machine-learning concepts, shortlisted noble-metal-free catalysts for selective ethane dehydrogenation. The predicted Ni3Mo alloy was synthesized and experimentally shown to outperform Pt in selective ethylene production. The machine-learning role is secondary to the descriptor-based workflow, and the evidence is a single catalyst test.
ai_technology: Descriptor-based microkinetic modeling with high-throughput DFT and machine learning
organization: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (SUNCAT); Westlake University; Lanzhou Institute of Chemical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: COVID Moonshot uses synthesis-directed de novo design for SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors
summary: A machine-learning de novo design model was coupled with synthesis route prediction in the COVID Moonshot campaign against the SARS-CoV-2 main protease. The authors report novel chemical scaffolds that are active in biochemical and live-virus assays and were synthesized along model-generated routes. The abstract gives no potency figures, so the strength of the result should be checked in the full text.
ai_technology: Synthesis-directed de novo design model with synthesis route prediction
organization: PostEra Inc.; University of Cambridge; The COVID Moonshot Consortium; University of Chicago; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; Weizmann Institute of Science

title: Machine learning guides automated synthesis of 19F MRI copolymer agents
summary: An automated continuous-flow polymer platform synthesized 397 copolymer compositions in a six-variable space, in iterative cycles guided by machine learning. Exploring under 0.9% of the compositional space, the models identified more than ten copolymers that outperformed state-of-the-art 19F MRI agents. Validation is experimental across hundreds of real syntheses, but the imaging performance claims are limited to the compositions tested.
ai_technology: Machine learning models guiding automated flow copolymer synthesis
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: An automated flow-synthesis platform made 397 copolymer compositions in a six-variable space; 10 compositions outperformed state-of-the-art 19F MRI agents.
evidence.unknown: In vivo imaging performance is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning guided iterative synthesis cycles and identified non-intuitive design criteria.

title: Interpretable machine learning discovers ultrapermeable polymer membranes for gas separation
summary: Multitask machine-learning models trained on experimental gas permeability data screened over 9 million hypothetical polymers. They identified hundreds of never-before-seen ultrapermeable membranes, with molecular dynamics simulations confirming the predicted permeabilities of the top candidates. The validation is computational rather than fabricated membranes, so the candidates remain unproven experimentally.
ai_technology: Multitask machine learning with model interpretation, plus molecular dynamics
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of Connecticut

title: Global methane point sources mapped from EMIT imaging spectroscopy with a vision transformer
summary: The MAPL-EMIT vision transformer uses full EMIT radiance spectra to jointly retrieve methane enhancements, plume outlines and source locations across global scenes, trained on 3.6 million synthetic plumes. The paper reports high recall and precision and better detection of weak plumes than matched-filter methods, but the abstract shows only synthetic evaluation; real-plume validation is not confirmed from the abstract.
ai_technology: MAPL-EMIT (end-to-end vision transformer on EMIT hyperspectral radiance)
organization: Google Research; Carnegie Institution for Science; Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology

title: Vision transformer detects methane point-source plumes in Sentinel-2 imagery at global scale
summary: A vision transformer applied to multispectral Sentinel-2 data detects methane plumes as small as 0.01 km2, corresponding to sources of about 200 to 300 kg CH4 per hour, and is reported to improve on the prior state of the art by an order of magnitude. Detections were compared with airborne methane measurement campaigns; the claims rest on that comparison and the abstract gives no formal detection-rate metrics.
ai_technology: Vision transformer for multispectral methane plume detection (Sentinel-2)

title: Quake Neural Operator builds microseismic catalogues without phase picking
summary: The Quake Neural Operator detects and locates microseismic events directly from continuous data without explicit phase picking. Applied to the Geysers geothermal field, it finds nearly an order of magnitude more seismic detections than routine catalogues, checked against the Phase Neural Operator and visual inspection rather than an independent ground-truth catalogue.
ai_technology: Quake Neural Operator (QNO), multi-task neural operator for classification and regression
organization: University of Texas at El Paso, Department of Earth, Environmental and Resource Sciences

title: Simulated training data locates archaeological tar-kiln-like sites in Louisiana, field check finds WWII features
summary: Machine learning models trained on simulated landscape data flagged 9 of 12 known targets (model 1) and all 12 (model 2, with 686 false positives among 709 remaining predictions) in Kisatchie National Forest, Louisiana; a model trained on real South Carolina tar kilns found 11 of 12. Field visits to 11 targets and augering of 2 found none of the expected tar-kiln features, and the authors concluded the structures more likely relate to a WWII military training site. Evidence caveat: only 12 known targets, and field validation is qualitative.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifiers trained on simulated archaeological sites (with a real tar-kiln-trained comparison model)
organization: University of New Mexico; New Mexico Consortium; Utah State University; Louisiana State University

title: Empirical Research Assistance writes expert-level scientific code across six domains
summary: Google's Empirical Research Assistance (ERA), a Gemini-based tree-search system, reaches expert-level performance on six benchmarks spanning genomics, public health, satellite imagery, neuroscience, time-series forecasting and mathematics. Its state-level U.S. hospital admission forecasts for flu, COVID-19 and RSV rank at or near the top of CDC leaderboards. Results are computational and checked against public benchmarks and leaderboards, with no wet-lab validation; exact benchmark scores were not visible in the sources read.
ai_technology: Empirical Research Assistance (ERA), Gemini-based tree search

title: Quine ranks compounds that shift pancreatic cancer cells toward a basal state
summary: Microsoft's Quine, a multimodal biology world model, prioritized thousands of compounds for shifting tumor cell states, and a handful were tested in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines. The top-ranked compounds produced the largest classical-to-basal shifts, as validated by wet-lab experiments, and some moved cells toward a distinct third phenotype. The post gives no quantitative wet-lab figures and links no paper, and it measures cell-state changes rather than clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Quine, multimodal biology world model with interactive harness
organization: Microsoft Research; Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT

title: Claude's Cycles: a Hamiltonian cycle decomposition found by Claude
summary: Knuth's note reports that Claude Opus 4.6 found an explicit decomposition of the arcs of the m^3-vertex digraph into three directed Hamiltonian cycles for odd m, an open problem Knuth posed. Knuth's proof of the construction was reportedly formally verified in Lean by Kim Morrison. Caveat: sources disagree on the even case, which an independent arXiv paper (2603.24708) and a GPT-5.4 Pro proof treat differently.

title: New Zarankiewicz numbers and bounds from OpenEvolve search
summary: Using the open-source OpenEvolve LLM-driven evolutionary framework with a custom reward, the authors find exact values Z(11,21,3,3)=116, Z(11,22,3,3)=121 and Z(12,22,3,3)=132, and lower bounds for 41 further parameter sets, at under $30 per case. Caveats: arXiv preprint not peer reviewed; a separate NeurIPS 2026 listing by overlapping authors reports different counts.
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; ETH Zurich; Stanford University

title: Co-FunSearch finds adversarial instances raising the Best-Fit bin packing bound
summary: A human-LLM pipeline (Co-FunSearch) finds adversarial instances for heuristics, raising the lower bound for Best-Fit bin packing in the random-order model from 1.3 to 1.5. The authors prove the 3/2 ratio analytically and report a search-found instance scoring 1.497 over 10,000 random shuffles against Packingsolver optima. Caveat: arXiv preprint; human analysis supplies the final proofs.
organization: University of Bonn; Google DeepMind; University of Manitoba

title: Anderson's 2014 commutative algebra problem resolved by Rethlas and Archon
summary: An informal reasoning agent (Rethlas) and a formal verification agent (Archon) resolve an open problem in commutative algebra posed by D. D. Anderson in 2014, as a counterexample. The Lean 4 formalization has about 19,450 lines and was produced in roughly 80 agent hours, with the code public on GitHub. Caveat: arXiv preprint; the Lean check covers the formal statement as written.
ai_technology: Rethlas (informal agent) with Archon (formal Lean agent)
organization: Peking University; Westlake University; Kyoto University; Tianjin University

title: Erdős Problem #650 solved with ChatGPT strategy and Aristotle Lean proof
summary: The authors prove f(m) = min(m, ceil(2 sqrt(m))) for all m, resolving Erdős Problem #650 on Bloom's site, where f(m) counts disjoint divisibility pairs in an interval for an m-element set. The detailed argument was formally verified in Lean by Harmonic's Aristotle, following a strategy proposed by ChatGPT. Caveat: arXiv preprint; the AI contribution is the strategy and formalization, not an independently checked autonomous solution.

title: EchoNet-Dynamic: video-based AI for left ventricular ejection fraction
summary: A deep learning model trained on echocardiogram videos segmented the left ventricle with a Dice coefficient of 0.92 and estimated ejection fraction with a mean absolute error of 4.1% (6.0% on an external dataset from another health system). Prospective evaluation with repeated human measurements found its variance comparable to or lower than that of human experts. Caveat: training data come from one institution's echocardiograms, with external testing on a single additional system.

title: Neural network ensemble for prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease
summary: An ensemble of neural networks trained on 107,823 fetal ultrasound images reached an AUC of 0.99, 95% sensitivity and 96% specificity in an internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys with 0.9% CHD. Its sensitivity was comparable to that of clinicians and it stayed robust on outside-hospital and lower-quality images. Caveat: retrospective study with a low-prevalence internal test set.
ai_technology: Ensemble of convolutional neural networks with segmentation models
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Trained on 107,823 images from 1,326 retrospective studies; on 4,108 fetal surveys (0.9% CHD), AUC 0.99, 95% sensitivity, 96% specificity, 100% negative predictive value; comparable to clinicians and robust on outside-hospital images.
evidence.unknown: Prospective screening performance is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of neural networks identifies cardiac views and classifies normal versus complex congenital heart disease.

title: Federated learning model predicts oxygen needs in COVID-19 patients
summary: The EXAM federated model, trained on data from 20 institutes without sharing patient data, achieved an average AUC above 0.92 for predicting oxygen requirements at 24 and 72 hours. At the largest independent test site it reached sensitivity 0.950 and specificity 0.882, with a 16% average AUC gain over single-site models. Caveat: retrospective data from the pandemic period and unharmonized sites.
ai_technology: EXAM federated learning model (EMR data and chest X-rays)
organization: University of Toronto; NVIDIA; Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; NYU Grossman School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Data from 20 institutes; average AUC above 0.92 for oxygen-requirement outcomes at 24 and 72 hours, 16% higher average AUC than single-site models; at the largest independent site, sensitivity 0.950 and specificity 0.882 for ventilation or death at 24 hours.
evidence.unknown: Effect on patient care when used in practice is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: EXAM, a model trained by federated learning on vital signs, laboratory data and chest X-rays without exchanging data between sites.

title: Deep learning reads HIV rapid tests photographed in rural South Africa
summary: Deep learning models trained on 11,374 smartphone-tablet images of HIV lateral-flow tests, captured by 60 fieldworkers, classified results with 97.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity in a pilot field study compared with human visual reading. The approach also reduced false positives and false negatives relative to human readers. Caveat: a pilot deployment in one rural setting, so wider field validation is still needed.
ai_technology: Deep learning image classifier on mobile-captured rapid test images
organization: Africa Health Research Institute; University College London

title: Deep learning assesses heart allograft rejection from biopsy whole-slide images
summary: A deep learning system analysing gigapixel endomyocardial biopsy slides detected allograft rejection with an AUC of 0.962, distinguished cellular and antibody-mediated rejection (AUCs 0.958 and 0.874) and graded rejection with an AUC of 0.833. In a human reader study it was non-inferior to conventional assessment and reduced interobserver variability and assessment time. Caveat: test cohorts from the US, Turkey and Switzerland are retrospective and the authors call for clinical trials.
ai_technology: Deep learning on whole-slide images for endomyocardial biopsies
organization: Harvard Medical School; Ege University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; University of California San Diego

title: Swarm learning predicts colorectal cancer mutations from histopathology slides
summary: Swarm learning, which trains models across partner sites without moving patient data, was applied to over 5,000 patients to predict BRAF status and microsatellite instability from H&E colorectal cancer slides. Swarm-trained models outperformed most locally trained models and matched models trained on merged datasets, and were validated on two independent UK datasets. Caveat: the outcome is a research-grade prediction from slides, not a clinical test.
ai_technology: Swarm learning with deep learning on histopathology images
organization: University of Oxford; Belfast Health and Social Care Trust; University of Leeds

title: Machine learning model predicts mental health crises from health records
summary: A model using electronic health records to flag patients at risk of a mental health crisis over 28 days reached an AUROC of 0.797, with 58% sensitivity at 85% specificity. A six-month prospective study in clinical practice found its predictions useful for managing caseloads or mitigating risk in 64% of cases. Caveat: modest precision (AUPRC 0.159), and one co-author is from the company that built the tool.
ai_technology: Machine learning model on electronic health records
organization: Koa Health; University of Warwick; Universitat Pompeu Fabra; Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

title: AI detects Parkinson's disease from nocturnal breathing signals
summary: An attention-based AI model extracting breathing from radio waves during sleep detected Parkinson's disease with an AUC of 0.90 on held-out data and 0.85 on external sets, across 7,671 individuals. Its severity estimates correlated with MDS-UPDRS scores (R = 0.94), and it worked for at-home assessment. Caveat: largely retrospective data and no prospective diagnostic trial reported.
ai_technology: Attention-based deep learning on contactless radio-wave breathing signals
organization: Mayo Clinic; University of Rochester Medical Center; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: Spectroscopic confirmation of neural-network lens candidates from DESI imaging
summary: A residual neural network selected strong gravitational lens candidates in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. VLT/MUSE spectroscopy of 76 candidates (223 spectra) confirmed 55 lenses with both lens and source redshifts, 15 with lens redshift only, and found 6 non-lenses. Caveat: the source is an arXiv preprint (submitted 22 September 2025) that does not name the network architecture or list institutions on its abstract page.
ai_technology: residual neural network (convolutional classifier for strong lens candidates)

title: Polybot: an autonomous lab finds processing recipes for conductive polymer films
summary: An AI-driven automated laboratory at Argonne used importance-guided Bayesian optimization to explore a seven-dimensional processing space for electronic polymer thin films. The campaign produced scale-up recipes for transparent conductive films with average conductivity above 4,500 S/cm, and feature-importance analysis identified key processing factors. Nature Communications abstract read; the number of experiments and the baseline comparison were not checked.
ai_technology: Importance-guided Bayesian optimization with automated synthesis and characterization
organization: Argonne National Laboratory; University of Chicago

evidence.tested: An autonomous campaign in a seven-dimensional processing space gave scale-up recipes for transparent conductive films averaging above 4,500 S/cm.
evidence.unknown: The number of experiments and the comparison with manual optimization are not given in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: Polybot, an automated laboratory driven by importance-guided Bayesian optimization.

title: FlowER predicts reaction mechanisms while conserving mass and electrons
summary: A flow-matching generative model represents reactions as electron redistribution in bond-electron matrices, so predicted products conserve both mass and electrons. The authors report that it avoids hallucinated atoms, recovers mechanistic steps for unseen substrate scaffolds and generalizes to new reaction classes with little fine-tuning. Computational results on reaction datasets (Nature abstract read); no new reactions were run in the lab.

evidence.tested: Exact mass and electron conservation, recovery of mechanistic sequences for unseen substrate scaffolds and generalization to out-of-domain reaction classes with little fine-tuning.
evidence.unknown: No laboratory validation of new reactions is reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: FlowER, a flow-matching generative model on bond-electron matrices.

title: GlaViTU maps glaciers worldwide close to expert accuracy
summary: A convolutional-transformer model maps glacier outlines from open satellite imagery, with intersection over union above 0.85 on unseen images in most cases, above 0.75 in debris-rich areas such as High-Mountain Asia and above 0.90 where clean ice dominates. Compared with human expert uncertainty it approaches or matches expert delineation; adding radar data improves accuracy. A benchmark covering 9% of the world's glaciers is released. Nature Communications abstract read.
organization: University of Twente; University of Oslo

evidence.tested: Intersection over union above 0.85 on unseen images in most cases, above 0.75 in debris-rich areas and above 0.90 where clean ice dominates; approaches or matches expert delineation uncertainty.
evidence.unknown: Whether it has been adopted in glacier inventories is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: GlaViTU, a convolutional-transformer model; a benchmark covering 9% of glaciers was released.
